text:
Meanwhile, other solvers on this problem proposed answers, and each answer was handed to a team of agents that was told it is the answer and asked to prove it completely, as a team, with a Slack channel and a shared workspace. What came of them:

e2: told that the answer is \mathcal D=\{(n,c)\in\mathbb Z_{\ge2}\times\mathbb Z_{\ge1}:n\ge3,\ c\ge3\}. Their run ended (all agents idle, the judge found the proof complete) after $3.94. What they established:

## Result and scope

The team established the proposed answer:
\[
\boxed{\mathcal D=\{(n,c):n\ge3,\ c\ge3\}.}
\]
Their proof uses explicitly declared structural theorems, not Python alone. In particular, they **invoke rather than reprove** integral degree-two Johnson injectivity, and standard results of Magnus, Nielsen, Matsumoto, Bass–Heller–Swan, and local reciprocity. They did not obtain a verified bibliographic citation for the integral Johnson theorem and deliberately avoided attributing it incorrectly.

No finding contradicts the proposed answer. Several early approaches failed, but an eventual stable metaplectic detector supplied strictness for all required ranks and degrees.

## General reduction and equality cases

Strong centrality,
\[
[\mathcal A_r(n),\mathcal A_s(n)]\subseteq\mathcal A_{r+s}(n),
\]
gives \(\gamma_c(\operatorname{IA}_n)\subseteq\mathcal A_c(n)\). The degree-\(c\) Johnson homomorphism therefore induces
\[
\tau_c:\gamma_c(\operatorname{IA}_n)/\gamma_{c+1}(\operatorname{IA}_n)
\longrightarrow \operatorname{Hom}(H,L_{c+1}(H)).
\]
The required strictness is exactly noninjectivity of this map. General reduction notes are in `workspace/agent1_general_reduction.txt`.

* **\(c=1\), all \(n\):** Magnus generators have first Johnson images forming the signed standard basis of \(H^*\otimes\Lambda^2H\). Since they generate \(\operatorname{IA}_n\), its abelianization is precisely this free abelian group. Thus
  \[
  \mathcal A_2(n)=\gamma_2(\operatorname{IA}_n).
  \]

* **\(c=2\), all \(n\):** The proof invokes the classical **integral** statement
  \[
  \tau_2:\gamma_2(\operatorname{IA}_n)/\gamma_3(\operatorname{IA}_n)
  \hookrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}(H,L_3(H)).
  \]
  Together with the preceding equality, this gives \(\mathcal A_3(n)=\gamma_3(\operatorname{IA}_n)\). The team did not complete an independent general-rank relator proof; finite bracket-rank calculations are supporting checks, not a replacement for this theorem.

* **\(n=2\), every \(c\):** An explicit Nielsen-generator calculation gives \(\operatorname{IA}_2=\operatorname{Inn}(F_2)\). The free-Lie centralizer argument gives
  \[
  Z(F_2/\gamma_{r+1}F_2)=\gamma_rF_2/\gamma_{r+1}F_2,
  \]
  hence \(\mathcal A_r(2)=\gamma_r(\operatorname{IA}_2)\). Details and exact free-word checks are in `workspace/agent4_n2_proof.txt` and `workspace/agent4_n2_checks.py`.

## Explicit witnesses for strictness

Use Magnus automorphisms
\[
K_{12}:x_1\mapsto x_2x_1x_2^{-1},\qquad
C_{i;jk}:x_i\mapsto[x_j,x_k]x_i,
\]
fixing the other generators. Put \(D=K_{12}\), \(A=C_{1;23}\), \(B=C_{3;12}\), and, for \(c\ge3\), define
\[
w_c=[D,[A,\operatorname{ad}_D^{\,c-3}B]],
\qquad \operatorname{ad}_D(g)=[D,g].
\]
Certainly \(w_c\in\gamma_c(\operatorname{IA}_n)\).

Its initial Johnson derivation vanishes integrally. Writing \(X=X_1,Y=X_2,Z=X_3\) and \(T=\operatorname{ad}Y\), the relevant derivations are
\[
D(X)=TX,\qquad A(X)=TZ,\qquad B(Z)=-TX.
\]
The derivation \(\operatorname{ad}_D^kB\) sends \(Z\) to \(-T^{k+1}X\); its bracket with \(A\) is diagonal on \(X,Z\), with entries \(T^{k+2},-T^{k+2}\), and commutes with \(D\). Therefore
\[
w_c\in\gamma_c(\operatorname{IA}_n)\cap\mathcal A_{c+1}(n).
\]

The difficult step was proving \(w_c\notin\gamma_{c+1}\), uniformly in \(n\).

## Stable detector

Take the character \(F_n\to\mathbb Z\) sending \(x_2\) to \(1\) and all other generators to \(0\). Its kernel’s abelianization is a free module over
\[
R=\mathbb Z[t,t^{-1}]
\]
of rank \(n-1\), giving an honest Alexander representation of \(\operatorname{IA}_n\).

In the final **column convention**, with \(s=t-1\), the relevant matrices are
\[
D=\operatorname{diag}(t,1),\quad A=E_{21}(s),\quad B=E_{12}(-s).
\]
Exactly,
\[
\operatorname{ad}_D^kB=E_{12}(-s^{k+1}).
\]
Gaussian factorization of the inner commutator has torus parameter \(1+s^{c-1}\), with remaining root factors of depth at least \(c\).

Balance determinants using an auxiliary coordinate and pass to stable elementary matrices. Bass–Heller–Swan gives
\[
K_2(R)\cong(\mathbb Z/2)^2,
\]
generated by \(\{-1,-1\}\) and \(\{-1,t\}\). Consequently specialization into a suitable local-field Hilbert-symbol cover descends to a genuine homomorphism: odd-order Hilbert symbols kill this kernel; for quadratic symbols, choose a field containing \(i\).

For an odd prime \(p\mid c\), take the totally ramified field defined by
\[
\Phi_p(1+\pi^{c/p})=0.
\]
For powers of two \(c\ge4\), use
\[
\pi^{c/2}-2\pi^{c/4}+2=0.
\]
These have residue field \(\mathbb F_p\), contain \(\mu_p\), and satisfy \(pe/(p-1)=c\). Critical local unit pairing gives
\[
(1+\pi,1+\pi^{c-1})_p\ne1.
\]

The team proved the needed filtration lemma by root/torus collection: above depth \(c\), the metaplectic cover splits, its split deep subgroup is normal, and quotienting by depth \(c+1\) produces a nilpotent group of class at most \(c\), retaining the central \(\mu_p\). Opposite-root corrections involve symbols \((1+ab,\pm a)_p\); these vanish beyond the threshold because sufficiently deep units are \(p\)-th powers.

In that quotient, \(w_c\) equals the nontrivial critical Hilbert symbol, up to inversion. Thus it cannot belong to \(\gamma_{c+1}\).

## Code, checks, and unsuccessful routes

The preferred full strictness write-up is `workspace/agent3_metaplectic_final.txt`. Filtration proofs also appear in `agent2_metaplectic_filtration.txt` and `agent4_metaplectic_filtration.txt`.

Executed exact checks include:

* `agent2_first_johnson.py`: Magnus basis calculations, \(n=2,\ldots,8\).
* `agent3_stable_symbolic_checks.py`, `agent4_column_word_checks.py`: conjugation, Gaussian identities, word valuations and Johnson cancellation, through \(c=20\).
* `agent2_hilbert_checks.py`, `agent2_odd_hilbert_checks.py`: actual quadratic and odd Hilbert-symbol examples.
* `agent3_odd_hilbert_norm_checks.py`, `agent4_odd_hilbert_norm_checks.py`: independent resultant/norm checks through prime \(19\).

Finite nilpotent, congruence, and logarithmic detectors initially failed; they did not disprove strictness. A separate dihedral quotient proves rank-three strictness, but did not stabilize. Speculative cyclic-homology/K-theory formulas were abandoned rather than used. Older `agent3_metaplectic_route.txt` notes are superseded by the final write-up. The scripts validate explicit algebra and examples; the declared structural theorems remain mathematical inputs.

e3: told that the answer is \mathcal D=\{(n,c)\in\mathbb Z_{\ge2}\times\mathbb Z_{\ge1}:n\ge3,\ c\ge4\}. Their run ended (all agents idle, the nudges used up) after $4.33. What they established:

## Main conclusion: the supplied answer is contradicted

The team ultimately proved
\[
(3,3)\in\mathcal D,
\]
although the prescribed answer excludes it. This is an explicit counterexample, not an inference from numerical ranks. Its membership and nonmembership were checked by independent implementations and then proved by hand.

### 1. The counterexample

Write \(F_3=\langle x,y,z\rangle\). Define automorphisms fixing generators not explicitly mentioned:
\[
\begin{array}{ll}
a:x\mapsto yxy^{-1},& b:x\mapsto zxz^{-1},\\
m:x\mapsto [y,z]x,& d:y\mapsto xyx^{-1},\\
e:y\mapsto [x,z]y.&
\end{array}
\]
All belong to \(\operatorname{IA}_3\). With the problem’s commutator convention, put
\[
u=[ [a,e],m]^3
  [[a,m],e]^{-1}
  [[a,b],b]^{-4}
  [[b,m],d]^{-2}.
\]
Plainly \(u\in\gamma_3(\operatorname{IA}_3)\). The team proved
\[
u\in\mathcal A_4(3),\qquad
u\notin\gamma_4(\operatorname{IA}_3).
\]

### 2. Why \(u\in\mathcal A_4(3)\)

The standard central-filtration property gives
\(\gamma_r(\operatorname{IA}_n)\subseteq\mathcal A_r(n)\). The degree-\(r\) Johnson map records the action modulo \(\mathcal A_{r+1}\), with values in degree-\(r\) derivations of the free Lie ring; it respects brackets.

Number the relevant Magnus generators as
\[
(g_0,g_1,g_2,g_3,g_5)=(a,b,m,d,e),
\]
and let \(D_{ijk}=[[D_i,D_j],D_k]\), where \(D_i\) is the first Johnson derivation. The exact integral identity is
\[
3D_{052}-D_{025}-4D_{011}-2D_{123}=0.
\]
It is precisely the degree-three Johnson image of \(u\).

A short hand verification was obtained. In the free Lie ring set
\[
k=[x,y],\quad w=[y,z],\quad h=[x,z],
\]
\[
P=[[k,z],z],\quad Q=[[w,z],x],\quad
R=[w,h],\quad S=[[h,z],y],\quad T=[[w,y],z].
\]
The derivations \(D_{052},D_{025},D_{011},D_{123}\), listed by their values on \((x,y,z)\), are respectively
\[
(-P+Q-R,T,0),\quad(-S-R,T,0),\quad
(Q,0,0),\quad(-P,T,0).
\]
Jacobi and Leibniz give \(S=P+Q+2R\), proving the identity.

Independently, literal substitution of the **92 signed Magnus generators** comprising \(u\), over the integers in truncated noncommutative Magnus series, fixed every generator through degree four. Thus this check concerned the actual automorphism, not merely tangent vectors.

### 3. Why \(u\notin\gamma_4(\operatorname{IA}_3)\)

They constructed a genuine homomorphism
\[
\operatorname{IA}_3\longrightarrow
H\longrightarrow \operatorname{UT}_4(\mathbb F_2),
\]
where
\[
H\cong C_2*C_2*C_2=\langle A,B,C\mid A^2=B^2=C^2=1\rangle.
\]

For the first map, take the abelianized Fox Jacobian evaluated at all variables \(-1\). **Convention matters:** row Jacobians are antihomomorphisms, so use the Jacobian of the inverse automorphism. These matrices fix \((1,1,1)\); quotienting by that vector and projectivizing gives a level-two subgroup of \(\operatorname{PGL}_2(\mathbb Z)\).

The whole projective level-two subgroup is generated by
\[
A(z)=-z,\qquad B(z)=2-z,\qquad C(z)=\frac z{2z-1}.
\]
Containment for the entire IA group—not just the displayed generators—was audited. An even-Euclidean-algorithm argument proves generation. Ping-pong on
\[
(-\infty,0),\quad(1,\infty),\quad(0,1)
\]
proves the free-product presentation. The five automorphism images are
\[
(a,b,m,d,e)\mapsto(B,A,AB,C,AC).
\]

Now map
\[
A\mapsto I+E_{12},\qquad
B\mapsto I+E_{34},\qquad
C\mapsto I+E_{23}.
\]
In this target, the three correction commutators in \(u\) are trivial, while
\[
[[B,AC],AB]=I+E_{14}.
\]
Consequently \(u\mapsto I+E_{14}\ne I\). Since \(\operatorname{UT}_4(\mathbb F_2)\) has class three, \(\gamma_4\) maps trivially. This proves the counterexample.

## Other established results

* **Formal reduction:** the defect in the question is the kernel of the integral graded Johnson map
  \[
  \gamma_c(\operatorname{IA}_n)/\gamma_{c+1}(\operatorname{IA}_n)
  \longrightarrow\operatorname{Der}_c(L_n).
  \]
  Image ranks alone do not prove injectivity.

* **Rank two:** \(\mathcal A_r(2)=\gamma_r(\operatorname{IA}_2)\) for every \(r\). They used \(\operatorname{IA}_2=\operatorname{Inn}(F_2)\) and
  \(Z(F_2/\gamma_{r+1})=\gamma_r/\gamma_{r+1}\). The latter follows from the common-centralizer argument in the free associative algebra.

* **All ranks, \(c=1\):** Magnus generators map to a signed basis of
  \(\operatorname{Hom}(H,\Lambda^2H)\), proving \(\mathcal A_2=\gamma_2\).

* **Rank three, all \(c\ge3\):** the reflection-algebra detector gives propagation. The cubic witness has leading polynomial
  \[
  ACB+CAB+BAC+BCA
  \]
  in \(\mathbb F_2\langle A,B,C\rangle/(A^2,B^2,C^2)\). Successive brackets appending \(C,B,C,B,\ldots\) preserve the coefficient of the word beginning \(ACB\). Hence nonzero Johnson-kernel classes occur in every subsequent degree.

## Workspace and computational certificates

The principal reproducible files are:

* `workspace/agent1_cubic_direct.py`
* `workspace/agent3_cubic_independent.py` — independent source, Fox-target, and finite-target checks.
* `workspace/agent4_degree3_direct.py`
* `workspace/agent2_cubic_target.py`, `agent4_cubic_target.py`
* `workspace/agent2_ut4_independent.py`, `agent4_ut4.py` — exhaustive target checks; lower-central orders \(64,8,2,1\).
* `workspace/agent4_n2.md`, `agent4_tensor.py`, `agent4_verify.py` — rank-two and filtration proofs/checks.
* `workspace/agent1_degree1.py` — degree-one checks.
* `workspace/agent4_rank3.md`, `agent4_seed_verify.py`, `agent3_propagation.md` — earlier quartic seed and propagation.

## What remains unresolved

They did **not** determine the actual complete set \(\mathcal D\). General-rank \(c=2,3\) and strictness for \(n\ge4\) remain unresolved. Reported integral \(c=2\) certificates cover \(n=3,\ldots,6\), using true-relator lattices with unit pivots (`agent2_c2_hnf.py`, associated relation JSON files); the proposed all-rank support reduction was withdrawn.

No graded rank-retraction or stabilization theorem was proved. Higher-rank individual and simultaneous sign-Fox congruence detectors lost the rank-three seed. Rational/modular Johnson-image computations likewise cannot certify source-group injectivity. None of these gaps weakens the explicit contradiction at \((3,3)\).

Each team's workspace is in experiments/<its id>/, next to your scratchpad: your runs can read it, not write it.

### agent3_metaplectic_final.txt 
 Strictness proof (all n>=3,c>=3), with standard background inputs explicitly named.

Inputs: Magnus generation and Magnus-Witt free Lie theorem; Bass-Heller-Swan K1(Z[t^+-1])={+-t^k}, K2=(Z/2)^2 generated {-1,-1},{-1,t}; stable Steinberg central extension and Matsumoto field-symbol relations; local Hilbert reciprocity filtration theorem. All other steps below are explicit.

Put X=x1,Y=x2,Z=x3. D=K12, A=C1;23, B=C3;12, with Kij(xi)=xj xi xj^-1 and Ci;jk(xi)=[xj,xk]xi. Let B_k=ad_D^k B in the group and w_c=[D,[A,B_{c-3}]]. This is in gamma_c(IA_n). On the free Lie algebra put T=ad Y. Degree-one derivations satisfy D(X)=TX, A(X)=TZ, B(Z)=-TX. Inductively (ad_D^k B)(Z)=-T^{k+1}X and [A,ad_D^kB] is diagonal on (X,Z), with images T^{k+2}X and -T^{k+2}Z. It commutes with D. Hence the degree-c Johnson image of w_c is zero and w_c lies A_{c+1}.

Use chi:F_n->Z sending x2->1 and other generators0. IA_n preserves chi. For N=ker chi, N_ab is a free R=Z[t,t^-1] module with basis xi, i!=2. IA acts R-linearly since phi(x2)x2^-1 lies N and inner conjugation by N is trivial on N_ab. In honest column-matrix convention on coordinates (x1,x3), images are D=diag(t,1), A=E21(s), B=E12(-s), s=t-1. Other coordinates are fixed for these elements. Therefore B_k=E12(-s^{k+1}) exactly. The full image lies I mod s.

Fix c. If c has an odd prime divisor p, k=c/p and let K/Qp be generated by pi with Eisenstein polynomial Phi_p(1+X^k), so residue Fp, e=(p-1)k, zeta_p=1+pi^k. If c is a power of2, c>=4, put d=c/4 and take pi with Eisenstein polynomial X^{2d}-2X^d+2; then residue F2,e=c/2,and i=1-pi^d. In either case mu_p subset K and C=pe/(p-1)=c. Specialize t=1+pi. The Hilbert pairing is trivial (U_r,U_s)_p if r+s>c, and U_{c+1} consists of pth powers. The induced pairing U1/U2 times U_{c-1}/Uc is perfect; both spaces are 1-dimensional over Fp. Consequently (1+pi,1+pi^{c-1})_p !=1.

Balance determinant by an extra coordinate: g -> diag(g,det(g)^-1). Because SK1(R)=0, this maps into stable E(R). Lift through St(R), specialize to St(K), push central K2(K) through the pth Hilbert symbol to mu_p. Ambiguity K2(R) dies: for oddp it is 2torsion; for p2, -1 is square in K so both {-1,-1},{-1,t} die. Thus there is a genuine hom from IA_n into the mu_p-cover of stable SL(K), lying over principal congruence Gamma1. A finite rank SL_M(K), M>=3, suffices for all matrices; stable field K2 agrees with Matsumoto K2 in such rank.

Filtered-cover lemma: write Gamma_r=ker(SL_M(O)->SL_M(O/pi^r)). For r<=c take F_r full preimage Gamma_r. For r>c let F_r be generated by canonical root lifts x_alpha(pi^r O) and canonical torus lifts h_alpha(U_r), WITHOUT central mu_p. Gaussian collection shows F_r->Gamma_r is isomorphic for r>c: torus symbols involve (U_r,U_r), and opposite-root symbols involve (1+ab,a), with 1+ab in U_{2r}; all vanish. Unique Gaussian normal form then excludes central kernel. The same four root cases show F_r normal in F_1 for r>c and [F_r,F_s] subset F_{r+s} for all r,s>=1: nonopposite roots give product parameter ab; torus-root gives (u^k-1)a; torus-torus gives Hilbert(U_r,U_s); opposite-root Gauss has pivot1+ab in U_{r+s}, with central symbols (1+ab, arbitrary). If r+s>c these symbols vanish (pivot is a pth power); if r+s<=c the assertion is automatic from matrix congruence because F_{r+s} is full preimage. Deep normality lets pair-generator commutator bounds extend to all products. Therefore Q=F1/F_{c+1} has nilpotency class at most c and retains central mu_p injectively.

Word evaluation in Q: let i,j be the module coordinates x1,x3 and ell the determinant-balancing coordinate. D stabilizes to torus h_{i,ell}(t). Set k=c-3. In the coordinate order (j,i), the inner commutator [A,B_k] is the standard opposite-root commutator with a=s,b=-s^{k+1}, ab=-s^{c-1}. Exact Gauss formula is
[x(a),y(b)]=x(-a^2 b/(1-ab)) h((1-ab)^-1) y(ab^2/(1-ab)).
Here d=1-ab=1+s^{c-1}; both root corrections have depth at least c. On commuting with D, these roots go to depth at least c+1 and die in Q. Any central ambiguity in the inner Gauss formula also dies on taking outer commutator. The remaining torus commutator is the Hilbert symbol (t,d)^{+-1}, since the coroots (i,ell),(j,i) have Cartan pairing -1. Thus w_c has central image (1+pi,1+pi^{c-1})_p^{+-1}, which is nontrivial. Since gamma_{c+1}(Q)=1, w_c cannot be in gamma_{c+1}(IA_n).

This proves gamma_{c+1}(IA_n) is strictly contained in gamma_c(IA_n) intersect A_{c+1}(n) for EVERY n>=3,c>=3.

### agent2_metaplectic_filtration.txt 
 Metaplectic congruence filtration lemma.
Let K be a nonarchimedean local field containing mu_p, O its valuation ring, pi a uniformizer, and C=p v_K(p)/(p-1). Let 1 -> mu_p -> H -> SL_infinity(K) -> 1 be the central extension obtained by pushing the stable Steinberg extension out through the Hilbert p-symbol. Assume (-1,x)_p=1 (automatic for odd p, and for p=2 when i is in K). Put U_r=1+pi^r O and Gamma_r=ker(SL_infinity(O)->SL_infinity(O/pi^r)).

Use canonical root lifts x_ij(a), and standard torus lifts h_i,ell(u). The field Steinberg relations imply:
(i) root subgroups are additive; nonopposite root commutators have product parameter ab;
(ii) torus-root conjugation is the ordinary root-weight scaling;
(iii) torus commutators are Hilbert symbols, with exponent the integral Cartan pairing;
(iv) opposite-root Gaussian collection has possible central factor a Dennis-Stein symbol, whose Hilbert image is (1+ab,+-a)_p (with harmless inverse/sign according to conventions).
All signs in (iv) are harmless here since (-1,x)_p=1.

Local reciprocity gives (U_r,U_s)_p=1 when r+s>C, and U_{C+1} is contained in K^{*p}.
For r>C, define F_r to be the subgroup generated by x_ij(pi^r O) and h_i,ell(U_r), without adjoining mu_p. Gaussian collection gives F_r -> Gamma_r is an isomorphism: all cross-root pivots are in U_{2r}, hence are p-th powers, so (iv) contributes no center; torus symbols (iii) also vanish. Thus collection is exactly ordinary LDU collection, with unique normal form. In particular F_r intersects mu_p trivially.
For r<=C define F_r to be the full inverse image of Gamma_r.

Each deep F_r (r>C) is normalized by F_1. Verify this on the above generating roots and tori: nonopposite-root and torus-root commutators have parameter in pi^{r+1}; opposite-root pivots are in U_{r+1}, hence p-th powers; torus pairs U_r,U_1 have total depth>C. No central discrepancy remains.
More generally, if r+s>C, the same generator check yields [F_r,F_s] <= F_{r+s}: opposite-root pivots 1+ab lie in U_{r+s} and hence are p-th powers; torus pairs U_r,U_s pair trivially. multiplicativity of sigma. In these assertions all roots and tori appearing

in this quotient (sigma sends identity to identity).

## Outcome

The team **did not prove the supplied classification**. They first proved its exclusion claims for \(n=2\) and for \(c\le2\). Later, however, they obtained an explicit, extensively checked counterexample at
\[
\boxed{(n,c)=(3,4)}.
\]
Thus their final substantive findings contradict the asserted answer. The agents’ last replies saying “no further cases” are stale: substantial later work in the channel supersedes them.

All paths below are relative to `workspace/`.

## Structural reduction and proved exclusions

They established the standard graded Johnson map
\[
J_c:\gamma_c(\operatorname{IA}_n)/\gamma_{c+1}(\operatorname{IA}_n)
\longrightarrow
\operatorname{Hom}\bigl(H,\gamma_{c+1}(F_n)/\gamma_{c+2}(F_n)\bigr),
\]
where \(H=F_n^{\mathrm{ab}}\), with kernel
\[
\frac{\gamma_c(\operatorname{IA}_n)\cap\mathcal A_{c+1}(n)}
{\gamma_{c+1}(\operatorname{IA}_n)}.
\]
Consequently, membership in \(\mathcal D\) is precisely failure of injectivity of \(J_c\). They justified the filtration identities, including \([\mathcal A_r,\mathcal A_s]\subseteq\mathcal A_{r+s}\), using commutator calculus and the three-subgroup lemma.

**Rank two, every degree.** Using classical Nielsen generation and a presentation of \(\mathrm{GL}_2(\mathbb Z)\), they proved \(\operatorname{IA}_2=\operatorname{Inn}(F_2)\cong F_2\). Exact reduced-word checks verified the required lifted presentation relations. Magnus–Witt and the trivial positive-degree center of the free Lie ring then give

Strong centrality,
\[
[\mathcal A_r(n),\mathcal A_s(n)]\subseteq\mathcal A_{r+s}(n),
\]
gives \(\gamma_c(\operatorname{IA}_n)\subseteq\mathcal A_c(n)\). The degree-\(c\) Johnson homomorphism therefore induces
\[
\tau_c:\gamma_c(\operatorname{IA}_n)/\gamma_{c+1}(\operatorname{IA}_n)
\longrightarrow \operatorname{Hom}(H,L_{c+1}(H)).
\]
The required strictness is exactly noninjectivity of this map. General reduction notes are in `workspace/agent1_general_reduction.txt`.

* **\(c=1\), all \(n\):** Magnus generators have first Johnson images forming the signed standard basis of \(H^*\otimes\Lambda^2H\). Since they generate \(\operatorname{IA}_n\), its abelianization is precisely this free abelian group. Thus

Use Magnus automorphisms

\qquad \operatorname{ad}_D(g)=[D,g].

Certainly \(w_c\in\gamma_c(\operatorname{IA}_n)\).

Its initial Johnson derivation vanishes integrally. Writing \(X=X_1,Y=X_2,Z=X_3\) and \(T=\operatorname{ad}Y\), the relevant derivations are
\[
D(X)=TX,\qquad A(X)=TZ,\qquad B(Z)=-TX.

The derivation \(\operatorname{ad}_D^kB\) sends \(Z\) to \(-T^{k+1}X\); its bracket with \(A\) is diagonal on \(X,Z\), with entries \(T^{k+2},-T^{k+2}\), and commutes with \(D\). Therefore
\[
w_c\in\gamma_c(\operatorname{IA}_n)\cap\mathcal A_{c+1}(n).

The difficult step was proving \(w_c\notin\gamma_{c+1}\), uniformly in \(n\).

## Stable detector

Take the character \(F_n\to\mathbb Z\) sending \(x_2\) to \(1\) and all other generators to \(0\). Its kernel’s abelianization is a free module over
\[
R=\mathbb Z[t,t^{-1}]
\]
of rank \(n-1\), giving an honest Alexander representation of \(\operatorname{IA}_n\).

In the final **column convention**, with \(s=t-1\), the relevant matrices are
\[
D=\operatorname{diag}(t,1),\quad A=E_{21}(s),\quad B=E_{12}(-s).
\]
Exactly,
\[
\operatorname{ad}_D^kB=E_{12}(-s^{k+1}).
\]
Gaussian factorization of the inner commutator has torus parameter \(1+s^{c-1}\), with remaining root factors of depth at least \(c\).

Balance determinants using an auxiliary coordinate and pass to stable elementary matrices. Bass–Heller–Swan gives
\[
K_2(R)\cong(\mathbb Z/2)^2,
\]
generated by \(\{-1,-1\}\) and \(\{-1,t\}\). Consequently specialization into a suitable local-field Hilbert-symbol cover descends to a genuine homomorphism: odd-order Hilbert symbols kill this kernel; for quadratic symbols, choose a field containing \(i\).

For an odd prime \(p\mid c\), take the totally ramified field defined by
\[
\Phi_p(1+\pi^{c/p})=0.
\]
For powers of two \(c\ge4\), use
\[
\pi^{c/2}-2\pi^{c/4}+2=0.
\]
These have residue field \(\mathbb F_p\), contain \(\mu_p\), and satisfy \(pe/(p-1)=c\). Critical local unit pairing gives
\[
(1+\pi,1+\pi^{c-1})_p\ne1.
\]

The team proved the needed filtration lemma by root/torus collection: above depth \(c\), the metaplectic cover splits, its split deep subgroup is normal, and quotienting by depth \(c+1\) produces a nilpotent group of class at most \(c\), retaining the central \(\mu_p\). Opposite-root corrections involve symbols \((1+ab,\pm a)_p\); these vanish beyond the threshold because sufficiently deep units are \(p\)-th powers.

In that quotient, \(w_c\) equals the nontrivial critical Hilbert symbol, up to inversion. Thus it cannot belong to \(\gamma_{c+1}\).

## Main conclusion: the supplied answer is contradicted

The team ultimately proved
\[
(3,3)\in\mathcal D,
\]
although the prescribed answer excludes it. This is an explicit counterexample, not an inference from numerical ranks. Its membership and nonmembership were checked by independent implementations and then proved by hand.

### 1. The counterexample

Write \(F_3=\langle x,y,z\rangle\). Define automorphisms fixing generators not explicitly mentioned:
\[
\begin{array}{ll}
a:x\mapsto yxy^{-1},& b:x\mapsto zxz^{-1},\\
m:x\mapsto [y,z]x,& d:y\mapsto xyx^{-1},\\
e:y\mapsto [x,z]y.&
\end{array}
\]
All belong to \(\operatorname{IA}_3\). With the problem’s commutator convention, put
\[
u=[ [a,e],m]^3
  [[a,m],e]^{-1}
  [[a,b],b]^{-4}
  [[b,m],d]^{-2}.
\]
Plainly \(u\in\gamma_3(\operatorname{IA}_3)\). The team proved
\[
u\in\mathcal A_4(3),\qquad
u\notin\gamma_4(\operatorname{IA}_3).
\]

### 2. Why \(u\in\mathcal A_4(3)\)

The standard central-filtration property gives
\(\gamma_r(\operatorname{IA}_n)\subseteq\mathcal A_r(n)\). The degree-\(r\) Johnson map records the action modulo \(\mathcal A_{r+1}\), with values in degree-\(r\) derivations of the free Lie ring; it respects brackets.

Number the relevant Magnus generators as
\[
(g_0,g_1,g_2,g_3,g_5)=(a,b,m,d,e),
\]
and let \(D_{ijk}=[[D_i,D_j],D_k]\), where \(D_i\) is the first Johnson derivation. The exact integral identity is
\[
3D_{052}-D_{025}-4D_{011}-2D_{123}=0.
\]
It is precisely the degree-three Johnson image of \(u\).

A short hand verification was obtained. In the free Lie ring set
\[
k=[x,y],\quad w=[y,z],\quad h=[x,z],
\]
\[
P=[[k,z],z],\quad Q=[[w,z],x],\quad
R=[w,h],\quad S=[[h,z],y],\quad T=[[w,y],z].
\]
The derivations \(D_{052},D_{025},D_{011},D_{123}\), listed by their values on \((x,y,z)\), are respectively
\[
(-P+Q-R,T,0),\quad(-S-R,T,0),\quad
(Q,0,0),\quad(-P,T,0).
\]
Jacobi and Leibniz give \(S=P+Q+2R\), proving the identity.

Independently, literal substitution of the **92 signed Magnus generators** comprising \(u\), over the integers in truncated noncommutative Magnus series, fixed every generator through degree four. Thus this check concerned the actual automorphism, not merely tangent vectors.

### 3. Why \(u\notin\gamma_4(\operatorname{IA}_3)\)

They constructed a genuine homomorphism
\[
\operatorname{IA}_3\longrightarrow
H\longrightarrow \operatorname{UT}_4(\mathbb F_2),
\]
where
\[
H\cong C_2*C_2*C_2=\langle A,B,C\mid A^2=B^2=C^2=1\rangle.
\]

For the first map, take the abelianized Fox Jacobian evaluated at all variables \(-1\). **Convention matters:** row Jacobians are antihomomorphisms, so use the Jacobian of the inverse automorphism. These matrices fix \((1,1,1)\); quotienting by that vector and projectivizing gives a level-two subgroup of \(\operatorname{PGL}_2(\mathbb Z)\).

The whole projective level-two subgroup is generated by
\[
A(z)=-z,\qquad B(z)=2-z,\qquad C(z)=\frac z{2z-1}.
\]
Containment for the entire IA group—not just the displayed generators—was audited. An even-Euclidean-algorithm argument proves generation. Ping-pong on
\[
(-\infty,0),\quad(1,\infty),\quad(0,1)
\]
proves the free-product presentation. The five automorphism images are
\[
(a,b,m,d,e)\mapsto(B,A,AB,C,AC).
\]

Now map
\[
A\mapsto I+E_{12},\qquad
B\mapsto I+E_{34},\qquad
C\mapsto I+E_{23}.
\]
In this target, the three correction commutators in \(u\) are trivial, while
\[
[[B,AC],AB]=I+E_{14}.
\]
Consequently \(u\mapsto I+E_{14}\ne I\). Since \(\operatorname{UT}_4(\mathbb F_2)\) has class three, \(\gamma_4\) maps trivially. This proves the counterexample.

## Other established results

* **Formal reduction:** the defect in the question is the kernel of the integral graded Johnson map
  \[
  \gamma_c(\operatorname{IA}_n)/\gamma_{c+1}(\operatorname{IA}_n)
  \longrightarrow\operatorname{Der}_c(L_n).
  \]
  Image ranks alone do not prove injectivity.

* **Rank two:** \(\mathcal A_r(2)=\gamma_r(\operatorname{IA}_2)\) for every \(r\). They used \(\operatorname{IA}_2=\operatorname{Inn}(F_2)\) and
  \(Z(F_2/\gamma_{r+1})=\gamma_r/\gamma_{r+1}\). The latter follows from the common-centralizer argument in the free associative algebra.

* **All ranks, \(c=1\):** Magnus generators map to a signed basis of
  \(\operatorname{Hom}(H,\Lambda^2H)\), proving \(\mathcal A_2=\gamma_2\).

* **Rank three, all \(c\ge3\):** the reflection-algebra detector gives propagation. The cubic witness has leading polynomial
  \[
  ACB+CAB+BAC+BCA
  \]
  in \(\mathbb F_2\langle A,B,C\rangle/(A^2,B^2,C^2)\). Successive brackets appending \(C,B,C,B,\ldots\) preserve the coefficient of the word beginning \(ACB\). Hence nonzero Johnson-kernel classes occur in every subsequent degree.

They did **not** determine the actual complete set \(\mathcal D\). General-rank \(c=2,3\) and strictness for \(n\ge4\) remain unresolved. Since gamma_{c+1}(Q)=1, w_c cannot be in gamma_{c+1}(IA_n).

This proves gamma_{c+1}(IA_n) is strictly contained in gamma_c(IA_n) intersect A_{c+1}(n) for EVERY n>=3,c>=3.

Metaplectic congruence filtration lemma.
Let K be a nonarchimedean local field containing mu_p, O its valuation ring, pi a uniformizer, and C=p v_K(p)/(p-1). Let 1 -> mu_p -> H -> SL_infinity(K) -> 1 be the central extension obtained by pushing the stable Steinberg extension out through the Hilbert p-symbol. Assume (-1,x)_p=1 (automatic for odd p, and for p=2 when i is in K). Put U_r=1+pi^r O and Gamma_r=ker(SL_infinity(O)->SL_infinity(O/pi^r)).

Use canonical root lifts x_ij(a), and standard torus lifts h_i,ell(u). The field Steinberg relations imply:
(i) root subgroups are additive; nonopposite root commutators have product parameter ab;
(ii) torus-root conjugation is the ordinary root-weight scaling;
(iii) torus commutators are Hilbert symbols, with exponent the integral Cartan pairing;
(iv) opposite-root Gaussian collection has possible central factor a Dennis-Stein symbol, whose Hilbert image is (1+ab,+-a)_p (with harmless inverse/sign according to conventions).
All signs in (iv) are harmless here since (-1,x)_p=1.

Local reciprocity gives (U_r,U_s)_p=1 when r+s>C, and U_{C+1} is contained in K^{*p}.
For r>C, define F_r to be the subgroup generated by x_ij(pi^r O) and h_i,ell(U_r), without adjoining mu_p. Gaussian collection gives F_r -> Gamma_r is an isomorphism: all cross-root pivots are in U_{2r}, hence are p-th powers, so (iv) contributes no center; torus symbols (iii) also vanish. Thus collection is exactly ordinary LDU collection, with unique normal form. In particular F_r intersects mu_p trivially.
For r<=C define F_r to be the full inverse image of Gamma_r.

Each deep F_r (r>C) is normalized by F_1. Verify this on the above generating roots and tori: nonopposite-root and torus-root commutators have parameter in pi^{r+1}; opposite-root pivots are in U_{r+1}, hence p-th powers; torus pairs U_r,U_1 have total depth>C. No central discrepancy remains.
More generally, if r+s>C, the same generator check yields [F_r,F_s] <= F_{r+s}: opposite-root pivots 1+ab lie in U_{r+s} and hence are p-th powers; torus pairs U_r,U_s pair trivially. If r+s<=C, the inclusion follows just from the ordinary matrix congruence commutator inclusion, as F_{r+s} is the full inverse image. Therefore (F_r) is an N-series.

Consequently Q=F_1/F_{C+1} is nilpotent of class at most C, and its central mu_p is still injective. All assertions hold in each finite rank >=3 and compatibly under stabilization. Q itself can be infinite-rank; each finitely generated image is a finite p-group since its projection is a congruence quotient over the finite ring O/pi^{C+1}.

CAVEAT FOR FINAL WRITEUP: relation (iv) and Gaussian uniqueness must be presented from the usual Steinberg/Dennis-Stein identities rather than assumed unexplained. The argument above gives the exact valuation verification once those standard identities are stated.


FILE experiments/e2/agent4_metaplectic_filtration.txt
Filtered metaplectic-cover lemma (root-calculus proof outline).

Let K be a nonarchimedean local field of characteristic zero containing mu_p,
O its integer ring, pi a uniformizer, e=v(p), C=pe/(p-1) an integer.
Write U_r=1+pi^r O and Gamma_r=ker(SL_N(O)->SL_N(O/pi^r)), N>=3.
Use the mu_p central extension of SL_N(K) obtained by pushing Matsumoto's
Steinberg extension through the p-th Hilbert symbol. It has standard root
lifts x_ij(a) and torus lifts h_ij(u).
The Hilbert unit theorem gives (U_i,U_j)_p=1 if i+j>C and U_{C+1}
subset (K^*)^p. The latter also annihilates symbols with arbitrary second argument.

Each g in Gamma_r has unique ordered LDU decomposition: root parameters
belong to pi^r O, diagonal parameters belong to U_r. Define sigma(g) by
using standard root lifts and a fixed ordered choice of torus lifts.
For r>C the map sigma restricted to Gamma_r is a homomorphism.
For g in Gamma_i and h in Gamma_j with i+j>C one has
 [sigma(g),sigma(h)] = sigma([g,h]).

Root-calculus verification: collect ordered root and torus factors. Root
addition has no central discrepancy. Nonopposite roots contribute a root
parameter ab, of valuation at least i+j. Torus/root interchange contributes
(u^k-1)a, likewise of valuation at least i+j. Torus/torus interchange
has discrepancy (u,v)_p raised to an integral Cartan coefficient,
u in U_i,v in U_j, hence is trivial beyond C. Opposite-root collection
uses the two-by-two Gaussian identity; its new diagonal unit is 1+ab in
U_{i+j}, and its central corrections are symbols involving 1+ab and a
or b (or their inverses). They vanish if i+j>C since U_{C+1} consists
of p-th powers. Subsequent collection of the new level-(i+j) factors has
no central errors by the same argument. This verifies the displayed identities.
For products wholly at level r>C, the identical calculation establishes
multiplicativity of sigma. In these assertions all roots and tori appearing
in original LDU factors retain their indicated valuation bounds.

Set F_r=the full preimage of Gamma_r when 1<=r<=C and
F_r=sigma(Gamma_r) for r>C. Then [F_i,F_j] subset F_{i+j}:
for i+j<=C it follows from matrix congruences; above C it follows from
root calculus. In particular sigma(Gamma_{C+1}) is normal in F_1,
F_1/sigma(Gamma_{C+1}) is nilpotent of class at most C, and mu_p embeds
in this quotient (sigma sends identity to identity).

The only inputs are Matsumoto's extension and the standard local Hilbert
unit-filtration theorem, plus the listed elementary Steinberg collection
relations. Any final proof should spell out the opposite-root lifted
Gaussian identity or cite its usual Steinberg-symbol version explicitly.

 Rank-three strictness, complete.
Write x1,x2,x3 for free generators. Set Kij(xi)=xj xi xj^{-1}, and Ci;jk(xi)=[xj,xk]xi; all other generators fixed. These are the nine Magnus generators of IA3.
Let d,e,f be degree-one derivations corresponding to K12,C1;23,C3;12. Their nonzero images are d(X1)=[X2,X1], e(X1)=[X2,X3], f(X3)=[X1,X2]. Set h=[e,f]. Then h(X1)=-[X2,[X1,X2]], h(X3)=[[X2,X3],X2], h(X2)=0. Direct derivation computation and Jacobi give [d,h]=0. Therefore w3=[K12,[C1;23,C3;12]] belongs gamma3(IA3) intersect A4(3). Define w_{c+1}=[K12,w_c]. Strong centrality gives w_c in gamma_c intersect A_{c+1} for every c>=3.

Detection in the infinite dihedral group:
The abelianized Fox Jacobian gives an antihomomorphism IA3 -> GL3(Z[t1^+-1,t2^+-1,t3^+-1]). Specialize all ti=-1. Every resulting matrix fixes (1,1,1)^T, by the Fox fundamental identity; quotient by this fixed line, using coordinates v1-v3,v2-v3, yields 2x2 matrices. Put
U=[[1,2],[0,1]], V=[[1,0],[2,1]], R=diag(-1,1), Z=-I.
In Magnus generator order K12,K13,C1;23,K21,K23,C2;13,K31,K32,C3;12, the matrices are
UR,R,U,ZVR,ZR,V,VR,ZUR,ZVU^{-1}.
Each identity is checked exactly in agent3_n3_checks.py. The subgroup <U,V> is free on U,V: on P1(R), put A={|z|>1}, B={|z|<1}; for every nonzero integer k, U^k(B) subset A and V^k(A) subset B. Ping-pong proves freeness and also excludes -I from <U,V>. R has determinant -1 and conjugates U,V to their inverses. Therefore <U,V,R,Z> is (F(U,V) semidirect C2_R) times C2_Z, with R inverting both free generators.
It has quotient D=<a,b | a^2=b^2=1> by U->a,V->b,R->1,Z->1. Inverting the row Jacobian first turns the antihomomorphism into a homomorphism q:IA3->D. On the nine Magnus generators q has images a,1,a,b,1,b,b,a,ab. Consequently q(w3)=[a,[a,ab]], equal (ab)^4 or its inverse depending on commutator convention; with the stated convention it is (ab)^4. In either case its exponent is +/-4.
Let z=ab. D is <z> semidirect <a>, with a z a=z^{-1}; its lower central series is gamma_c(D)=<z^{2^{c-1}}> for c>=2. Thus q(w3) is in gamma3(D) but not gamma4(D). Iterating [a,-] doubles the exponent up to sign, so q(w_c)=z^{+/-2^{c-1}} is not in gamma_{c+1}(D). It follows w_c not in gamma_{c+1}(IA3), proving strictness for n=3 and all c>=3.

No claim is made here about survival under IA3 -> IAn. That stabilization is unresolved in this team's work.

Meanwhile, other solvers on this problem proposed answers, and each answer was handed to a team of agents that was told it is the answer and asked to prove it completely, as a team, with a Slack channel and a shared workspace. What came of them:

e1: told that the answer is \mathcal D=\{(n,c)\in\mathbb Z_{\ge2}\times\mathbb Z_{\ge1}: n\ge3,\ c\ge6\}. Their run ended (budget ($20.02)) after $20.68. What they established:

## Outcome

The team **did not prove the supplied classification**. They first proved its exclusion claims for \(n=2\) and for \(c\le2\). Later, however, they obtained an explicit, extensively checked counterexample at
\[
\boxed{(n,c)=(3,4)}.
\]
Thus their final substantive findings contradict the asserted answer. The agents’ last replies saying “no further cases” are stale: substantial later work in the channel supersedes them.

All paths below are relative to `workspace/`.

## Structural reduction and proved exclusions

They established the standard graded Johnson map
\[
J_c:\gamma_c(\operatorname{IA}_n)/\gamma_{c+1}(\operatorname{IA}_n)
\longrightarrow
\operatorname{Hom}\bigl(H,\gamma_{c+1}(F_n)/\gamma_{c+2}(F_n)\bigr),
\]
where \(H=F_n^{\mathrm{ab}}\), with kernel
\[
\frac{\gamma_c(\operatorname{IA}_n)\cap\mathcal A_{c+1}(n)}
{\gamma_{c+1}(\operatorname{IA}_n)}.
\]
Consequently, membership in \(\mathcal D\) is precisely failure of injectivity of \(J_c\). They justified the filtration identities, including \([\mathcal A_r,\mathcal A_s]\subseteq\mathcal A_{r+s}\), using commutator calculus and the three-subgroup lemma.

**Rank two, every degree.** Using classical Nielsen generation and a presentation of \(\mathrm{GL}_2(\mathbb Z)\), they proved \(\operatorname{IA}_2=\operatorname{Inn}(F_2)\cong F_2\). Exact reduced-word checks verified the required lifted presentation relations. Magnus–Witt and the trivial positive-degree center of the free Lie ring then give
\[
\gamma_c(\operatorname{IA}_2)\cap\mathcal A_{c+1}(2)
=\gamma_{c+1}(\operatorname{IA}_2).
\]
Files: `rank2_proof.md`, `rank2_certificate.py`.

**Degree one, every rank.** Magnus generators have first Johnson images forming a signed permutation basis of \(H^*\otimes\Lambda^2H\). Surjectivity from the free abelian group on these generators, followed by this unimodular map, proves
\[
\mathcal A_2(n)=\gamma_2(\operatorname{IA}_n).
\]
File: `degree1_certificate.py`; finite tests cover \(2\le n\le12\), while the indexing argument proves all ranks.

**Degree two, every rank.** They proved
\[
\mathcal A_3(n)=\gamma_3(\operatorname{IA}_n).
\]
The finite-rank certificates use genuine commuting automorphisms and Nielsen conjugation to generate the entire integral kernel of the derivation-bracket matrix. Primitivity is certified by Smith normal form, not rational ranks:

- \(n=3\): bracket rank \(18\); relation lattice primitive of rank \(18\).
- \(n=4\): bracket rank \(70\), kernel rank \(206\); relation closure grows \(118\to202\to206\), with all \(206\) Smith invariants equal to \(1\).

Run `degree2_certificate.py`, or with argument `4`. The lattice justification is in `agent3_degree2_lattice_lemma.md`.

The audited all-rank reduction is in `agent4_all_rank_degree2_proof.md`, independently discussed in `agent2_allrank_degree2_audit.md`. It uses exact same-target and dummy-index exchange identities, then weight-by-weight integral canonicalization on at most four labels. For positive weight \(a+b\), an independent “star” basis \(W_s,L_s,G\) replaces potentially troublesome graph-cycle arguments. Trace cancellation is proved symbolically, not inferred from tests. Supporting files include `agent4_degree2_relations.md`, `same_target_relation.py`, and `agent4_trace_certificate.py`.

A consolidated account of these exclusions is `agent1_verified_partial_proof.md`.

## Explicit contradiction at \((3,4)\)

Use zero-based free generators \(x_0,x_1,x_2\). Let
\[
K_{ij}:x_i\mapsto x_jx_ix_j^{-1},\qquad
C_{i;jk}:x_i\mapsto x_i[x_j,x_k],
\]
fixing other generators. Order the nine Magnus generators as
\[
(g_0,\ldots,g_8)=
(K_{01},K_{02},C_{0;12},
 K_{10},K_{12},C_{1;02},
 K_{20},K_{21},C_{2;01}).
\]
Define
\[
t(a,b,c,d)=[[[g_a,g_b],g_c],g_d^{-1}]
\]
and
\[
W=t(0,8,3,1)\,
t(0,8,3,4)\,
t(4,3,8,0)\,
t(4,7,8,3)^{-1}.
\]
This is an 88-letter Magnus-generator word, manifestly in \(\gamma_4(\operatorname{IA}_3)\).

Two independent exact **integer** truncated-Magnus computations verified that \(W\) acts identically through wordlength \(5\). Hence
\[
W\in\mathcal A_5(3).
\]
Files: `agent4_degree4_candidate_word.json`, `agent4_degree4_candidate_direct_check.py`, and the independent `agent3_explicit_W_check.py`/`.json`.

For nonmembership in \(\gamma_5\), they used the genuine finite action on
\[
\mathbb F_3\langle X_0,X_1,X_2\rangle/
(\text{monomials of degree}>8).
\]
In this image, \(\mathcal A_4\) is an additive elementary abelian group: corrections start in wordlength \(5\), so nonlinear composition terms disappear.

## Result and scope

The team established the proposed answer:
\[
\boxed{\mathcal D=\{(n,c):n\ge3,\ c\ge3\}.}
\]
Their proof uses explicitly declared structural theorems, not Python alone. In particular, they **invoke rather than reprove** integral degree-two Johnson injectivity, and standard results of Magnus, Nielsen, Matsumoto, Bass–Heller–Swan, and local reciprocity. They did not obtain a verified bibliographic citation for the integral Johnson theorem and deliberately avoided attributing it incorrectly.

No finding contradicts the proposed answer. Several early approaches failed, but an eventual stable metaplectic detector supplied strictness for all required ranks and degrees.

## General reduction and equality cases

Strong centrality,
\[
[\mathcal A_r(n),\mathcal A_s(n)]\subseteq\mathcal A_{r+s}(n),
\]
gives \(\gamma_c(\operatorname{IA}_n)\subseteq\mathcal A_c(n)\). The degree-\(c\) Johnson homomorphism therefore induces
\[
\tau_c:\gamma_c(\operatorname{IA}_n)/\gamma_{c+1}(\operatorname{IA}_n)
\longrightarrow \operatorname{Hom}(H,L_{c+1}(H)).
\]
The required strictness is exactly noninjectivity of this map. General reduction notes are in `workspace/agent1_general_reduction.txt`.

* **\(c=1\), all \(n\):** Magnus generators have first Johnson images forming the signed standard basis of \(H^*\otimes\Lambda^2H\). Since they generate \(\operatorname{IA}_n\), its abelianization is precisely this free abelian group. Thus
  \[
  \mathcal A_2(n)=\gamma_2(\operatorname{IA}_n).
  \]

* **\(c=2\), all \(n\):** The proof invokes the classical **integral** statement
  \[
  \tau_2:\gamma_2(\operatorname{IA}_n)/\gamma_3(\operatorname{IA}_n)
  \hookrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}(H,L_3(H)).
  \]
  Together with the preceding equality, this gives \(\mathcal A_3(n)=\gamma_3(\operatorname{IA}_n)\). The team did not complete an independent general-rank relator proof; finite bracket-rank calculations are supporting checks, not a replacement for this theorem.

* **\(n=2\), every \(c\):** An explicit Nielsen-generator calculation gives \(\operatorname{IA}_2=\operatorname{Inn}(F_2)\). The free-Lie centralizer argument gives
  \[
  Z(F_2/\gamma_{r+1}F_2)=\gamma_rF_2/\gamma_{r+1}F_2,
  \]
  hence \(\mathcal A_r(2)=\gamma_r(\operatorname{IA}_2)\). Details and exact free-word checks are in `workspace/agent4_n2_proof.txt` and `workspace/agent4_n2_checks.py`.

## Explicit witnesses for strictness

Use Magnus automorphisms
\[
K_{12}:x_1\mapsto x_2x_1x_2^{-1},\qquad
C_{i;jk}:x_i\mapsto[x_j,x_k]x_i,
\]
fixing the other generators. Put \(D=K_{12}\), \(A=C_{1;23}\), \(B=C_{3;12}\), and, for \(c\ge3\), define
\[
w_c=[D,[A,\operatorname{ad}_D^{\,c-3}B]],
\qquad \operatorname{ad}_D(g)=[D,g].
\]
Certainly \(w_c\in\gamma_c(\operatorname{IA}_n)\).

Its initial Johnson derivation vanishes integrally. Writing \(X=X_1,Y=X_2,Z=X_3\) and \(T=\operatorname{ad}Y\), the relevant derivations are
\[
D(X)=TX,\qquad A(X)=TZ,\qquad B(Z)=-TX.
\]
The derivation \(\operatorname{ad}_D^kB\) sends \(Z\) to \(-T^{k+1}X\); its bracket with \(A\) is diagonal on \(X,Z\), with entries \(T^{k+2},-T^{k+2}\), and commutes with \(D\). Therefore
\[
w_c\in\gamma_c(\operatorname{IA}_n)\cap\mathcal A_{c+1}(n).
\]

The difficult step was proving \(w_c\notin\gamma_{c+1}\), uniformly in \(n\).

## Stable detector

Take the character \(F_n\to\mathbb Z\) sending \(x_2\) to \(1\) and all other generators to \(0\). Its kernel’s abelianization is a free module over
\[
R=\mathbb Z[t,t^{-1}]
\]
of rank \(n-1\), giving an honest Alexander representation of \(\operatorname{IA}_n\).

In the final **column convention**, with \(s=t-1\), the relevant matrices are
\[
D=\operatorname{diag}(t,1),\quad A=E_{21}(s),\quad B=E_{12}(-s).
\]
Exactly,
\[
\operatorname{ad}_D^kB=E_{12}(-s^{k+1}).
\]
Gaussian factorization of the inner commutator has torus parameter \(1+s^{c-1}\), with remaining root factors of depth at least \(c\).

Balance determinants using an auxiliary coordinate and pass to stable elementary matrices. Bass–Heller–Swan gives
\[
K_2(R)\cong(\mathbb Z/2)^2,
\]
generated by \(\{-1,-1\}\) and \(\{-1,t\}\). Consequently specialization into a suitable local-field Hilbert-symbol cover descends to a genuine homomorphism: odd-order Hilbert symbols kill this kernel; for quadratic symbols, choose a field containing \(i\).

For an odd prime \(p\mid c\), take the totally ramified field defined by
\[
\Phi_p(1+\pi^{c/p})=0.
\]
For powers of two \(c\ge4\), use
\[
\pi^{c/2}-2\pi^{c/4}+2=0.
\]
These have residue field \(\mathbb F_p\), contain \(\mu_p\), and satisfy \(pe/(p-1)=c\). Critical local unit pairing gives
\[
(1+\pi,1+\pi^{c-1})_p\ne1.
\]

The team proved the needed filtration lemma by root/torus collection: above depth \(c\), the metaplectic cover splits, its split deep subgroup is normal, and quotienting by depth \(c+1\) produces a nilpotent group of class at most \(c\), retaining the central \(\mu_p\). Opposite-root corrections involve symbols \((1+ab,\pm a)_p\); these vanish beyond the threshold because sufficiently deep units are \(p\)-th powers.

In that quotient, \(w_c\) equals the nontrivial critical Hilbert symbol, up to inversion. Thus it cannot belong to \(\gamma_{c+1}\).

## Main conclusion: the supplied answer is contradicted

The team ultimately proved
\[
(3,3)\in\mathcal D,
\]
although the prescribed answer excludes it. This is an explicit counterexample, not an inference from numerical ranks. Its membership and nonmembership were checked by independent implementations and then proved by hand.

### 1. The counterexample

Write \(F_3=\langle x,y,z\rangle\). Define automorphisms fixing generators not explicitly mentioned:
\[
\begin{array}{ll}
a:x\mapsto yxy^{-1},& b:x\mapsto zxz^{-1},\\
m:x\mapsto [y,z]x,& d:y\mapsto xyx^{-1},\\
e:y\mapsto [x,z]y.&
\end{array}
\]
All belong to \(\operatorname{IA}_3\). With the problem’s commutator convention, put
\[
u=[ [a,e],m]^3
  [[a,m],e]^{-1}
  [[a,b],b]^{-4}
  [[b,m],d]^{-2}.
\]
Plainly \(u\in\gamma_3(\operatorname{IA}_3)\). The team proved
\[
u\in\mathcal A_4(3),\qquad
u\notin\gamma_4(\operatorname{IA}_3).
\]

### 2. Why \(u\in\mathcal A_4(3)\)

The standard central-filtration property gives
\(\gamma_r(\operatorname{IA}_n)\subseteq\mathcal A_r(n)\). The degree-\(r\) Johnson map records the action modulo \(\mathcal A_{r+1}\), with values in degree-\(r\) derivations of the free Lie ring; it respects brackets.

Number the relevant Magnus generators as
\[
(g_0,g_1,g_2,g_3,g_5)=(a,b,m,d,e),
\]
and let \(D_{ijk}=[[D_i,D_j],D_k]\), where \(D_i\) is the first Johnson derivation. The exact integral identity is
\[
3D_{052}-D_{025}-4D_{011}-2D_{123}=0.
\]
It is precisely the degree-three Johnson image of \(u\).

A short hand verification was obtained. In the free Lie ring set
\[
k=[x,y],\quad w=[y,z],\quad h=[x,z],
\]
\[
P=[[k,z],z],\quad Q=[[w,z],x],\quad
R=[w,h],\quad S=[[h,z],y],\quad T=[[w,y],z].
\]
The derivations \(D_{052},D_{025},D_{011},D_{123}\), listed by their values on \((x,y,z)\), are respectively
\[
(-P+Q-R,T,0),\quad(-S-R,T,0),\quad
(Q,0,0),\quad(-P,T,0).
\]
Jacobi and Leibniz give \(S=P+Q+2R\), proving the identity.

Independently, literal substitution of the **92 signed Magnus generators** comprising \(u\), over the integers in truncated noncommutative Magnus series, fixed every generator through degree four. Thus this check concerned the actual automorphism, not merely tangent vectors.

### 3. Why \(u\notin\gamma_4(\operatorname{IA}_3)\)

They constructed a genuine homomorphism
\[
\operatorname{IA}_3\longrightarrow
H\longrightarrow \operatorname{UT}_4(\mathbb F_2),
\]
where
\[
H\cong C_2*C_2*C_2=\langle A,B,C\mid A^2=B^2=C^2=1\rangle.
\]

For the first map, take the abelianized Fox Jacobian evaluated at all variables \(-1\). **Convention matters:** row Jacobians are antihomomorphisms, so use the Jacobian of the inverse automorphism. These matrices fix \((1,1,1)\); quotienting by that vector and projectivizing gives a level-two subgroup of \(\operatorname{PGL}_2(\mathbb Z)\).

The whole projective level-two subgroup is generated by
\[
A(z)=-z,\qquad B(z)=2-z,\qquad C(z)=\frac z{2z-1}.
\]
Containment for the entire IA group—not just the displayed generators—was audited. An even-Euclidean-algorithm argument proves generation. Ping-pong on
\[
(-\infty,0),\quad(1,\infty),\quad(0,1)
\]
proves the free-product presentation. The five automorphism images are
\[
(a,b,m,d,e)\mapsto(B,A,AB,C,AC).
\]

Now map
\[
A\mapsto I+E_{12},\qquad
B\mapsto I+E_{34},\qquad
C\mapsto I+E_{23}.
\]
In this target, the three correction commutators in \(u\) are trivial, while
\[
[[B,AC],AB]=I+E_{14}.
\]
Consequently \(u\mapsto I+E_{14}\ne I\). Since \(\operatorname{UT}_4(\mathbb F_2)\) has class three, \(\gamma_4\) maps trivially. This proves the counterexample.

## Other established results

* **Formal reduction:** the defect in the question is the kernel of the integral graded Johnson map
  \[
  \gamma_c(\operatorname{IA}_n)/\gamma_{c+1}(\operatorname{IA}_n)
  \longrightarrow\operatorname{Der}_c(L_n).
  \]
  Image ranks alone do not prove injectivity.

* **Rank two:** \(\mathcal A_r(2)=\gamma_r(\operatorname{IA}_2)\) for every \(r\). They used \(\operatorname{IA}_2=\operatorname{Inn}(F_2)\) and
  \(Z(F_2/\gamma_{r+1})=\gamma_r/\gamma_{r+1}\). The latter follows from the common-centralizer argument in the free associative algebra.

* **All ranks, \(c=1\):** Magnus generators map to a signed basis of
  \(\operatorname{Hom}(H,\Lambda^2H)\), proving \(\mathcal A_2=\gamma_2\).

* **Rank three, all \(c\ge3\):** the reflection-algebra detector gives propagation. The cubic witness has leading polynomial
  \[
  ACB+CAB+BAC+BCA
  \]
  in \(\mathbb F_2\langle A,B,C\rangle/(A^2,B^2,C^2)\). Successive brackets appending \(C,B,C,B,\ldots\) preserve the coefficient of the word beginning \(ACB\). Hence nonzero Johnson-kernel classes occur in every subsequent degree.

## What remains unresolved

They did **not** determine the actual complete set \(\mathcal D\). General-rank \(c=2,3\) and strictness for \(n\ge4\) remain unresolved. Reported integral \(c=2\) certificates cover \(n=3,\ldots,6\), using true-relator lattices with unit pivots (`agent2_c2_hnf.py`, associated relation JSON files); the proposed all-rank support reduction was withdrawn.

No graded rank-retraction or stabilization theorem was proved. Higher-rank individual and simultaneous sign-Fox congruence detectors lost the rank-three seed. Rational/modular Johnson-image computations likewise cannot certify source-group injectivity. None of these gaps weakens the explicit contradiction at \((3,3)\).

Meanwhile, other solvers on this problem proposed answers, and each answer was handed to a team of agents that was told it is the answer and asked to prove it completely, as a team, with a Slack channel and a shared workspace. What came of them:

e2: told that the answer is \mathcal D=\{(n,c)\in\mathbb Z_{\ge2}\times\mathbb Z_{\ge1}:n\ge3,\ c\ge3\}. Their run ended (all agents idle, the judge found the proof complete) after $3.94. What they established:

## Result and scope

The team established the proposed answer:
\[
\boxed{\mathcal D=\{(n,c):n\ge3,\ c\ge3\}.}
\]
Their proof uses explicitly declared structural theorems, not Python alone. In particular, they **invoke rather than reprove** integral degree-two Johnson injectivity, and standard results of Magnus, Nielsen, Matsumoto, Bass–Heller–Swan, and local reciprocity. They did not obtain a verified bibliographic citation for the integral Johnson theorem and deliberately avoided attributing it incorrectly.

No finding contradicts the proposed answer. Several early approaches failed, but an eventual stable metaplectic detector supplied strictness for all required ranks and degrees.

## General reduction and equality cases

Strong centrality,
\[
[\mathcal A_r(n),\mathcal A_s(n)]\subseteq\mathcal A_{r+s}(n),
\]
gives \(\gamma_c(\operatorname{IA}_n)\subseteq\mathcal A_c(n)\). The degree-\(c\) Johnson homomorphism therefore induces
\[
\tau_c:\gamma_c(\operatorname{IA}_n)/\gamma_{c+1}(\operatorname{IA}_n)
\longrightarrow \operatorname{Hom}(H,L_{c+1}(H)).
\]
The required strictness is exactly noninjectivity of this map. General reduction notes are in `workspace/agent1_general_reduction.txt`.

* **\(c=1\), all \(n\):** Magnus generators have first Johnson images forming the signed standard basis of \(H^*\otimes\Lambda^2H\). Since they generate \(\operatorname{IA}_n\), its abelianization is precisely this free abelian group. Thus
  \[
  \mathcal A_2(n)=\gamma_2(\operatorname{IA}_n).
  \]

* **\(c=2\), all \(n\):** The proof invokes the classical **integral** statement
  \[
  \tau_2:\gamma_2(\operatorname{IA}_n)/\gamma_3(\operatorname{IA}_n)
  \hookrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}(H,L_3(H)).
  \]
  Together with the preceding equality, this gives \(\mathcal A_3(n)=\gamma_3(\operatorname{IA}_n)\). The team did not complete an independent general-rank relator proof; finite bracket-rank calculations are supporting checks, not a replacement for this theorem.

* **\(n=2\), every \(c\):** An explicit Nielsen-generator calculation gives \(\operatorname{IA}_2=\operatorname{Inn}(F_2)\). The free-Lie centralizer argument gives
  \[
  Z(F_2/\gamma_{r+1}F_2)=\gamma_rF_2/\gamma_{r+1}F_2,
  \]
  hence \(\mathcal A_r(2)=\gamma_r(\operatorname{IA}_2)\). Details and exact free-word checks are in `workspace/agent4_n2_proof.txt` and `workspace/agent4_n2_checks.py`.

## Explicit witnesses for strictness

Use Magnus automorphisms
\[
K_{12}:x_1\mapsto x_2x_1x_2^{-1},\qquad
C_{i;jk}:x_i\mapsto[x_j,x_k]x_i,
\]
fixing the other generators. Put \(D=K_{12}\), \(A=C_{1;23}\), \(B=C_{3;12}\), and, for \(c\ge3\), define
\[
w_c=[D,[A,\operatorname{ad}_D^{\,c-3}B]],
\qquad \operatorname{ad}_D(g)=[D,g].
\]
Certainly \(w_c\in\gamma_c(\operatorname{IA}_n)\).

Its initial Johnson derivation vanishes integrally. Writing \(X=X_1,Y=X_2,Z=X_3\) and \(T=\operatorname{ad}Y\), the relevant derivations are
\[
D(X)=TX,\qquad A(X)=TZ,\qquad B(Z)=-TX.
\]
The derivation \(\operatorname{ad}_D^kB\) sends \(Z\) to \(-T^{k+1}X\); its bracket with \(A\) is diagonal on \(X,Z\), with entries \(T^{k+2},-T^{k+2}\), and commutes with \(D\). Therefore
\[
w_c\in\gamma_c(\operatorname{IA}_n)\cap\mathcal A_{c+1}(n).
\]

The difficult step was proving \(w_c\notin\gamma_{c+1}\), uniformly in \(n\).

## Stable detector

Take the character \(F_n\to\mathbb Z\) sending \(x_2\) to \(1\) and all other generators to \(0\). Its kernel’s abelianization is a free module over
\[
R=\mathbb Z[t,t^{-1}]
\]
of rank \(n-1\), giving an honest Alexander representation of \(\operatorname{IA}_n\).

In the final **column convention**, with \(s=t-1\), the relevant matrices are
\[
D=\operatorname{diag}(t,1),\quad A=E_{21}(s),\quad B=E_{12}(-s).
\]
Exactly,
\[
\operatorname{ad}_D^kB=E_{12}(-s^{k+1}).
\]
Gaussian factorization of the inner commutator has torus parameter \(1+s^{c-1}\), with remaining root factors of depth at least \(c\).

Balance determinants using an auxiliary coordinate and pass to stable elementary matrices. Bass–Heller–Swan gives
\[
K_2(R)\cong(\mathbb Z/2)^2,
\]
generated by \(\{-1,-1\}\) and \(\{-1,t\}\). Consequently specialization into a suitable local-field Hilbert-symbol cover descends to a genuine homomorphism: odd-order Hilbert symbols kill this kernel; for quadratic symbols, choose a field containing \(i\).

For an odd prime \(p\mid c\), take the totally ramified field defined by
\[
\Phi_p(1+\pi^{c/p})=0.
\]
For powers of two \(c\ge4\), use
\[
\pi^{c/2}-2\pi^{c/4}+2=0.
\]
These have residue field \(\mathbb F_p\), contain \(\mu_p\), and satisfy \(pe/(p-1)=c\). Critical local unit pairing gives
\[
(1+\pi,1+\pi^{c-1})_p\ne1.
\]

The team proved the needed filtration lemma by root/torus collection: above depth \(c\), the metaplectic cover splits, its split deep subgroup is normal, and quotienting by depth \(c+1\) produces a nilpotent group of class at most \(c\), retaining the central \(\mu_p\). Opposite-root corrections involve symbols \((1+ab,\pm a)_p\); these vanish beyond the threshold because sufficiently deep units are \(p\)-th powers.

In that quotient, \(w_c\) equals the nontrivial critical Hilbert symbol, up to inversion. Thus it cannot belong to \(\gamma_{c+1}\).

## Code, checks, and unsuccessful routes

The preferred full strictness write-up is `workspace/agent3_metaplectic_final.txt`. Filtration proofs also appear in `agent2_metaplectic_filtration.txt` and `agent4_metaplectic_filtration.txt`.

Executed exact checks include:

* `agent2_first_johnson.py`: Magnus basis calculations, \(n=2,\ldots,8\).
* `agent3_stable_symbolic_checks.py`, `agent4_column_word_checks.py`: conjugation, Gaussian identities, word valuations and Johnson cancellation, through \(c=20\).
* `agent2_hilbert_checks.py`, `agent2_odd_hilbert_checks.py`: actual quadratic and odd Hilbert-symbol examples.
* `agent3_odd_hilbert_norm_checks.py`, `agent4_odd_hilbert_norm_checks.py`: independent resultant/norm checks through prime \(19\).

Finite nilpotent, congruence, and logarithmic detectors initially failed; they did not disprove strictness. A separate dihedral quotient proves rank-three strictness, but did not stabilize. Speculative cyclic-homology/K-theory formulas were abandoned rather than used. Older `agent3_metaplectic_route.txt` notes are superseded by the final write-up. The scripts validate explicit algebra and examples; the declared structural theorems remain mathematical inputs.

e3: told that the answer is \mathcal D=\{(n,c)\in\mathbb Z_{\ge2}\times\mathbb Z_{\ge1}:n\ge3,\ c\ge4\}. Their run ended (all agents idle, the nudges used up) after $4.33. What they established:

## Main conclusion: the supplied answer is contradicted

The team ultimately proved
\[
(3,3)\in\mathcal D,
\]
although the prescribed answer excludes it. This is an explicit counterexample, not an inference from numerical ranks. Its membership and nonmembership were checked by independent implementations and then proved by hand.

### 1. The counterexample

Write \(F_3=\langle x,y,z\rangle\). Define automorphisms fixing generators not explicitly mentioned:
\[
\begin{array}{ll}
a:x\mapsto yxy^{-1},& b:x\mapsto zxz^{-1},\\
m:x\mapsto [y,z]x,& d:y\mapsto xyx^{-1},\\
e:y\mapsto [x,z]y.&
\end{array}
\]
All belong to \(\operatorname{IA}_3\). With the problem’s commutator convention, put
\[
u=[ [a,e],m]^3
  [[a,m],e]^{-1}
  [[a,b],b]^{-4}
  [[b,m],d]^{-2}.
\]
Plainly \(u\in\gamma_3(\operatorname{IA}_3)\). The team proved
\[
u\in\mathcal A_4(3),\qquad
u\notin\gamma_4(\operatorname{IA}_3).
\]

### 2. Why \(u\in\mathcal A_4(3)\)

The standard central-filtration property gives
\(\gamma_r(\operatorname{IA}_n)\subseteq\mathcal A_r(n)\). The degree-\(r\) Johnson map records the action modulo \(\mathcal A_{r+1}\), with values in degree-\(r\) derivations of the free Lie ring; it respects brackets.

Number the relevant Magnus generators as
\[
(g_0,g_1,g_2,g_3,g_5)=(a,b,m,d,e),
\]
and let \(D_{ijk}=[[D_i,D_j],D_k]\), where \(D_i\) is the first Johnson derivation. The exact integral identity is
\[
3D_{052}-D_{025}-4D_{011}-2D_{123}=0.
\]
It is precisely the degree-three Johnson image of \(u\).

A short hand verification was obtained. In the free Lie ring set
\[
k=[x,y],\quad w=[y,z],\quad h=[x,z],
\]
\[
P=[[k,z],z],\quad Q=[[w,z],x],\quad
R=[w,h],\quad S=[[h,z],y],\quad T=[[w,y],z].
\]
The derivations \(D_{052},D_{025},D_{011},D_{123}\), listed by their values on \((x,y,z)\), are respectively
\[
(-P+Q-R,T,0),\quad(-S-R,T,0),\quad
(Q,0,0),\quad(-P,T,0).
\]
Jacobi and Leibniz give \(S=P+Q+2R\), proving the identity.

Independently, literal substitution of the **92 signed Magnus generators** comprising \(u\), over the integers in truncated noncommutative Magnus series, fixed every generator through degree four. Thus this check concerned the actual automorphism, not merely tangent vectors.

### 3. Why \(u\notin\gamma_4(\operatorname{IA}_3)\)

They constructed a genuine homomorphism
\[
\operatorname{IA}_3\longrightarrow
H\longrightarrow \operatorname{UT}_4(\mathbb F_2),
\]
where
\[
H\cong C_2*C_2*C_2=\langle A,B,C\mid A^2=B^2=C^2=1\rangle.
\]

For the first map, take the abelianized Fox Jacobian evaluated at all variables \(-1\). **Convention matters:** row Jacobians are antihomomorphisms, so use the Jacobian of the inverse automorphism. These matrices fix \((1,1,1)\); quotienting by that vector and projectivizing gives a level-two subgroup of \(\operatorname{PGL}_2(\mathbb Z)\).

The whole projective level-two subgroup is generated by
\[
A(z)=-z,\qquad B(z)=2-z,\qquad C(z)=\frac z{2z-1}.
\]
Containment for the entire IA group—not just the displayed generators—was audited. An even-Euclidean-algorithm argument proves generation. Ping-pong on
\[
(-\infty,0),\quad(1,\infty),\quad(0,1)
\]
proves the free-product presentation. The five automorphism images are
\[
(a,b,m,d,e)\mapsto(B,A,AB,C,AC).
\]

Now map
\[
A\mapsto I+E_{12},\qquad
B\mapsto I+E_{34},\qquad
C\mapsto I+E_{23}.
\]
In this target, the three correction commutators in \(u\) are trivial, while
\[
[[B,AC],AB]=I+E_{14}.
\]
Consequently \(u\mapsto I+E_{14}\ne I\). Since \(\operatorname{UT}_4(\mathbb F_2)\) has class three, \(\gamma_4\) maps trivially. This proves the counterexample.

## Other established results

* **Formal reduction:** the defect in the question is the kernel of the integral graded Johnson map
  \[
  \gamma_c(\operatorname{IA}_n)/\gamma_{c+1}(\operatorname{IA}_n)
  \longrightarrow\operatorname{Der}_c(L_n).
  \]
  Image ranks alone do not prove injectivity.

* **Rank two:** \(\mathcal A_r(2)=\gamma_r(\operatorname{IA}_2)\) for every \(r\). They used \(\operatorname{IA}_2=\operatorname{Inn}(F_2)\) and
  \(Z(F_2/\gamma_{r+1})=\gamma_r/\gamma_{r+1}\). The latter follows from the common-centralizer argument in the free associative algebra.

* **All ranks, \(c=1\):** Magnus generators map to a signed basis of
  \(\operatorname{Hom}(H,\Lambda^2H)\), proving \(\mathcal A_2=\gamma_2\).

* **Rank three, all \(c\ge3\):** the reflection-algebra detector gives propagation. The cubic witness has leading polynomial
  \[
  ACB+CAB+BAC+BCA
  \]
  in \(\mathbb F_2\langle A,B,C\rangle/(A^2,B^2,C^2)\). Successive brackets appending \(C,B,C,B,\ldots\) preserve the coefficient of the word beginning \(ACB\). Hence nonzero Johnson-kernel classes occur in every subsequent degree.

## Workspace and computational certificates

The principal reproducible files are:

* `workspace/agent1_cubic_direct.py`
* `workspace/agent3_cubic_independent.py` — independent source, Fox-target, and finite-target checks.
* `workspace/agent4_degree3_direct.py`
* `workspace/agent2_cubic_target.py`, `agent4_cubic_target.py`
* `workspace/agent2_ut4_independent.py`, `agent4_ut4.py` — exhaustive target checks; lower-central orders \(64,8,2,1\).
* `workspace/agent4_n2.md`, `agent4_tensor.py`, `agent4_verify.py` — rank-two and filtration proofs/checks.
* `workspace/agent1_degree1.py` — degree-one checks.
* `workspace/agent4_rank3.md`, `agent4_seed_verify.py`, `agent3_propagation.md` — earlier quartic seed and propagation.

## What remains unresolved

They did **not** determine the actual complete set \(\mathcal D\). General-rank \(c=2,3\) and strictness for \(n\ge4\) remain unresolved. Reported integral \(c=2\) certificates cover \(n=3,\ldots,6\), using true-relator lattices with unit pivots (`agent2_c2_hnf.py`, associated relation JSON files); the proposed all-rank support reduction was withdrawn.

No graded rank-retraction or stabilization theorem was proved. Higher-rank individual and simultaneous sign-Fox congruence detectors lost the rank-three seed. Rational/modular Johnson-image computations likewise cannot certify source-group injectivity. None of these gaps weakens the explicit contradiction at \((3,3)\).

Each team's workspace is in experiments/<its id>/, next to your scratchpad: your runs can read it, not write it.

## agent3_metaplectic_final.txt 
 Strictness proof (all n>=3,c>=3), with standard background inputs explicitly named.

Inputs: Magnus generation and Magnus-Witt free Lie theorem; Bass-Heller-Swan K1(Z[t^+-1])={+-t^k}, K2=(Z/2)^2 generated {-1,-1},{-1,t}; stable Steinberg central extension and Matsumoto field-symbol relations; local Hilbert reciprocity filtration theorem. All other steps below are explicit.

Put X=x1,Y=x2,Z=x3. D=K12, A=C1;23, B=C3;12, with Kij(xi)=xj xi xj^-1 and Ci;jk(xi)=[xj,xk]xi. Let B_k=ad_D^k B in the group and w_c=[D,[A,B_{c-3}]]. This is in gamma_c(IA_n). On the free Lie algebra put T=ad Y. Degree-one derivations satisfy D(X)=TX, A(X)=TZ, B(Z)=-TX. Inductively (ad_D^k B)(Z)=-T^{k+1}X and [A,ad_D^kB] is diagonal on (X,Z), with images T^{k+2}X and -T^{k+2}Z. It commutes with D. Hence the degree-c Johnson image of w_c is zero and w_c lies A_{c+1}.

Use chi:F_n->Z sending x2->1 and other generators0. IA_n preserves chi. For N=ker chi, N_ab is a free R=Z[t,t^-1] module with basis xi, i!=2. IA acts R-linearly since phi(x2)x2^-1 lies N and inner conjugation by N is trivial on N_ab. In honest column-matrix convention on coordinates (x1,x3), images are D=diag(t,1), A=E21(s), B=E12(-s), s=t-1. Other coordinates are fixed for these elements. Therefore B_k=E12(-s^{k+1}) exactly. The full image lies I mod s.

Fix c. If c has an odd prime divisor p, k=c/p and let K/Qp be generated by pi with Eisenstein polynomial Phi_p(1+X^k), so residue Fp, e=(p-1)k, zeta_p=1+pi^k. If c is a power of2, c>=4, put d=c/4 and take pi with Eisenstein polynomial X^{2d}-2X^d+2; then residue F2,e=c/2,and i=1-pi^d. In either case mu_p subset K and C=pe/(p-1)=c. Specialize t=1+pi. The Hilbert pairing is trivial (U_r,U_s)_p if r+s>c, and U_{c+1} consists of pth powers. The induced pairing U1/U2 times U_{c-1}/Uc is perfect; both spaces are 1-dimensional over Fp. Consequently (1+pi,1+pi^{c-1})_p !=1.

Balance determinant by an extra coordinate: g -> diag(g,det(g)^-1). Because SK1(R)=0, this maps into stable E(R). Lift through St(R), specialize to St(K), push central K2(K) through the pth Hilbert symbol to mu_p. Ambiguity K2(R) dies: for oddp it is 2torsion; for p2, -1 is square in K so both {-1,-1},{-1,t} die. Thus there is a genuine hom from IA_n into the mu_p-cover of stable SL(K), lying over principal congruence Gamma1. A finite rank SL_M(K), M>=3, suffices for all matrices; stable field K2 agrees with Matsumoto K2 in such rank.

Filtered-cover lemma: write Gamma_r=ker(SL_M(O)->SL_M(O/pi^r)). For r<=c take F_r full preimage Gamma_r. For r>c let F_r be generated by canonical root lifts x_alpha(pi^r O) and canonical torus lifts h_alpha(U_r), WITHOUT central mu_p. Gaussian collection shows F_r->Gamma_r is isomorphic for r>c: torus symbols involve (U_r,U_r), and opposite-root symbols involve (1+ab,a), with 1+ab in U_{2r}; all vanish. Unique Gaussian normal form then excludes central kernel. The same four root cases show F_r normal in F_1 for r>c and [F_r,F_s] subset F_{r+s} for all r,s>=1: nonopposite roots give product parameter ab; torus-root gives (u^k-1)a; torus-torus gives Hilbert(U_r,U_s); opposite-root Gauss has pivot1+ab in U_{r+s}, with central symbols (1+ab, arbitrary). If r+s>c these symbols vanish (pivot is a pth power); if r+s<=c the assertion is automatic from matrix congruence because F_{r+s} is full preimage. Deep normality lets pair-generator commutator bounds extend to all products. Therefore Q=F1/F_{c+1} has nilpotency class at most c and retains central mu_p injectively.

Word evaluation in Q: let i,j be the module coordinates x1,x3 and ell the determinant-balancing coordinate. D stabilizes to torus h_{i,ell}(t). Set k=c-3. In the coordinate order (j,i), the inner commutator [A,B_k] is the standard opposite-root commutator with a=s,b=-s^{k+1}, ab=-s^{c-1}. Exact Gauss formula is
[x(a),y(b)]=x(-a^2 b/(1-ab)) h((1-ab)^-1) y(ab^2/(1-ab)).
Here d=1-ab=1+s^{c-1}; both root corrections have depth at least c. On commuting with D, these roots go to depth at least c+1 and die in Q. Any central ambiguity in the inner Gauss formula also dies on taking outer commutator. The remaining torus commutator is the Hilbert symbol (t,d)^{+-1}, since the coroots (i,ell),(j,i) have Cartan pairing -1. Thus w_c has central image (1+pi,1+pi^{c-1})_p^{+-1}, which is nontrivial. Since gamma_{c+1}(Q)=1, w_c cannot be in gamma_{c+1}(IA_n).

This proves gamma_{c+1}(IA_n) is strictly contained in gamma_c(IA_n) intersect A_{c+1}(n) for EVERY n>=3,c>=3.

Executable checks: agent3_stable_symbolic_checks.py (all-parameter root identities, Eisenstein choices c3..80, integral free-associative Johnson-zero family c3..20); agent4_column_word_checks.py (honest column convention and exact Laurent order); agent3_odd_hilbert_norm_checks.py (actual algebraic norm computation proving nontrivial odd-p Hilbert symbols for c=p=3,5,7,11,13,17,19); agent2_hilbert_checks.py (actual PARI quadratic local symbols).


## agent2_metaplectic_filtration.txt 
 Metaplectic congruence filtration lemma.
Let K be a nonarchimedean local field containing mu_p, O its valuation ring, pi a uniformizer, and C=p v_K(p)/(p-1). Let 1 -> mu_p -> H -> SL_infinity(K) -> 1 be the central extension obtained by pushing the stable Steinberg extension out through the Hilbert p-symbol. Assume (-1,x)_p=1 (automatic for odd p, and for p=2 when i is in K). Put U_r=1+pi^r O and Gamma_r=ker(SL_infinity(O)->SL_infinity(O/pi^r)).

Use canonical root lifts x_ij(a), and standard torus lifts h_i,ell(u). The field Steinberg relations imply:
(i) root subgroups are additive; nonopposite root commutators have product parameter ab;
(ii) torus-root conjugation is the ordinary root-weight scaling;
(iii) torus commutators are Hilbert symbols, with exponent the integral Cartan pairing;
(iv) opposite-root Gaussian collection has possible central factor a Dennis-Stein symbol, whose Hilbert image is (1+ab,+-a)_p (with harmless inverse/sign according to conventions).
All signs in (iv) are harmless here since (-1,x)_p=1.

Local reciprocity gives (U_r,U_s)_p=1 when r+s>C, and U_{C+1} is contained in K^{*p}.
For r>C, define F_r to be the subgroup generated by x_ij(pi^r O) and h_i,ell(U_r), without adjoining mu_p. Gaussian collection gives F_r -> Gamma_r is an isomorphism: all cross-root pivots are in U_{2r}, hence are p-th powers, so (iv) contributes no center; torus symbols (iii) also vanish. Thus collection is exactly ordinary LDU collection, with unique normal form. In particular F_r intersects mu_p trivially.
For r<=C define F_r to be the full inverse image of Gamma_r.

Each deep F_r (r>C) is normalized by F_1. Verify this on the above generating roots and tori: nonopposite-root and torus-root commutators have parameter in pi^{r+1}; opposite-root pivots are in U_{r+1}, hence p-th powers; torus pairs U_r,U_1 have total depth>C. No central discrepancy remains.
More generally, if r+s>C, the same generator check yields [F_r,F_s] <= F_{r+s}: opposite-root pivots 1+ab lie in U_{r+s} and hence are p-th powers; torus pairs U_r,U_s pair trivially. If r+s<=C, the inclusion follows just from the ordinary matrix congruence commutator inclusion, as F_{r+s} is the full inverse image. Therefore (F_r) is an N-series.

Consequently Q=F_1/F_{C+1} is nilpotent of class at most C, and its central mu_p is still injective. All assertions hold in each finite rank >=3 and compatibly under stabilization. Q itself can be infinite-rank; each finitely generated image is a finite p-group since its projection is a congruence quotient over the finite ring O/pi^{C+1}.

## agent4_metaplectic_filtration.txt 
 Filtered metaplectic-cover lemma (root-calculus proof outline).

Let K be a nonarchimedean local field of characteristic zero containing mu_p,
O its integer ring, pi a uniformizer, e=v(p), C=pe/(p-1) an integer.
Write U_r=1+pi^r O and Gamma_r=ker(SL_N(O)->SL_N(O/pi^r)), N>=3.
Use the mu_p central extension of SL_N(K) obtained by pushing Matsumoto's
Steinberg extension through the p-th Hilbert symbol. It has standard root
lifts x_ij(a) and torus lifts h_ij(u).
The Hilbert unit theorem gives (U_i,U_j)_p=1 if i+j>C and U_{C+1}
subset (K^*)^p. The latter also annihilates symbols with arbitrary second argument.

Each g in Gamma_r has unique ordered LDU decomposition: root parameters
belong to pi^r O, diagonal parameters belong to U_r. Define sigma(g) by
using standard root lifts and a fixed ordered choice of torus lifts.
For r>C the map sigma restricted to Gamma_r is a homomorphism.
For g in Gamma_i and h in Gamma_j with i+j>C one has
 [sigma(g),sigma(h)] = sigma([g,h]).

Root-calculus verification: collect ordered root and torus factors. Root
addition has no central discrepancy. Nonopposite roots contribute a root
parameter ab, of valuation at least i+j. Torus/root interchange contributes
(u^k-1)a, likewise of valuation at least i+j. Torus/torus interchange
has discrepancy (u,v)_p raised to an integral Cartan coefficient,
u in U_i,v in U_j, hence is trivial beyond C. Opposite-root collection
uses the two-by-two Gaussian identity; its new diagonal unit is 1+ab in
U_{i+j}, and its central corrections are symbols involving 1+ab and a
or b (or their inverses). They vanish if i+j>C since U_{C+1} consists
of p-th powers. Subsequent collection of the new level-(i+j) factors has
no central errors by the same argument. This verifies the displayed identities.
For products wholly at level r>C, the identical calculation establishes
multiplicativity of sigma. In these assertions all roots and tori appearing
in original LDU factors retain their indicated valuation bounds.

Set F_r=the full preimage of Gamma_r when 1<=r<=C and
F_r=sigma(Gamma_r) for r>C. Then [F_i,F_j] subset F_{i+j}:
for i+j<=C it follows from matrix congruences; above C it follows from
root calculus. In particular sigma(Gamma_{C+1}) is normal in F_1,
F_1/sigma(Gamma_{C+1}) is nilpotent of class at most C, and mu_p embeds
in this quotient (sigma sends identity to identity).

The only inputs are Matsumoto's extension and the standard local Hilbert
unit-filtration theorem, plus the listed elementary Steinberg collection
relations. Any final proof should spell out the opposite-root lifted
Gaussian identity or cite its usual Steinberg-symbol version explicitly.
