C-type has two distinct positive output labels. The only C-C columns
are E_ip=a(i;pa) wedge a(p;ia), i,p!=a, i!=p.
Put T_i=e_i^* [[i,a],a]. Their images are T_p-T_i.
Fix t!=a; the columns E_it (i!=a,t) have independent images.
Every E_ip=E_it+E_tp follows from rank4 injectivity on {a,i,p,t}.
Thus there is no kernel in this weight either.

These exhaust weights (sum of coordinates is two), proving
ker[Lambda^2(V)->Der_2]=relations in gr_2(IA_n), for every n.
Consequently gamma_2(IA_n) intersect A_3(n)=gamma_3(IA_n).
Together with the degree-one theorem this also gives A_3=gamma_3.

agent3_degree2_lattice_lemma.md # A finite integral certificate criterion for degree-two injectivity

Let G be a group, let V=G/[G,G] be free abelian of finite rank, and let
beta: Lambda^2 V -> gamma_2(G)/gamma_3(G)
be the canonical surjection, beta(u wedge v)=[u,v].
Let J: gamma_2(G)/gamma_3(G) -> W be a homomorphism to a free abelian group.
Suppose an integer matrix B represents J beta.

For each pair of commuting elements a,b in G, the column
[a]_ab wedge [b]_ab belongs to ker beta. More generally, if theta is any
automorphism of G, then theta_ab([a]_ab) wedge theta_ab([b]_ab) belongs
to ker beta, because theta(a),theta(b) still commute.

Form the integer matrix R whose columns are any such relations. If
(1) B R=0,
(2) rank_Q R = dim_Q ker B,
(3) every nonzero Smith invariant of R is 1,
then J is injective.

Proof: let N be the number of rows of R. Condition (3) says that
Z^N/im R is torsion-free, i.e. im R is saturated. Conditions (1),(2)
then imply im R=ker B: for x in ker B, equality of rational spans gives
a nonzero integer m with mx in im R; saturation gives x in im R.
Every R column is killed by beta, while ker beta is contained in ker B,
so ker beta=ker B. Therefore the induced J is injective. No presentation
of G, finiteness assumption on its relation set, or torsion-freeness
assumption on gamma_2(G)/gamma_3(G) is used.

For G=IA_n, V=H^* tensor Lambda^2 H by the Magnus-generator argument.
Take W=Hom(H,L_3(H)), or its canonical embedding in
Hom(H,H^{tensor 3}). Then B is the degree-two derivation bracket map.
The standard Johnson calculation identifies J with the restriction of
tau_2 to gamma_2(G). Therefore the three conditions prove
 gamma_2(IA_n) intersect A_3(n) = gamma_3(IA_n).
Combining with A_2(n)=gamma_2(IA_n) gives A_3(n)=gamma_3(IA_n).

CAUTION: rational ranks alone do not suffice: condition (3) is essential.

agent4_all_rank_degree2_proof.md # Integral degree-two Johnson injectivity in every rank

## Inputs

Use the proved degree-one identification IA_n^ab=V_n=Hom(H,L_2), with signed basis a_i;jk=e_i^* tensor [X_j,X_k], j!=k. For i in {j,k} its lift is a signed basis conjugation, otherwise a commutator transvection. Let q:Lambda^2 V_n -> gr_2(IA_n) be the surjective bracket map and B:Lambda^2 V_n -> Hom(H,L_3) the derivation bracket, so B=J_2 q.

The exact primitive-lattice certificates degree2_certificate.py prove J_2 injective for n=3,4; rank2 follows from rank2_proof.md. Consequently any z supported on at most four coordinate labels with Bz=0 has qz=0 in every rank: embed the corresponding smaller free-group automorphism group by fixing the extra generators. No injectivity of this group inclusion on lower-central quotients is required.

## Reduction of individual columns

The degree-one basis is multihomogeneous with weight e_j+e_k-e_i; hence Lambda^2 V is a direct sum of integral weight groups and B preserves weight. This is an algebraic multigrading; no assumption that weight-space decomposition follows from the integral diagonal torus is made.

Consider a wedge of two basis derivations. With different targets and no target occurring in the other's output pair, their Magnus lifts commute exactly. With the same target, if both are commutator transvections, their wedge is a true degree-two relation in all ranks by the partial-inner identity proved in agent4_degree2_relations.md. Every remaining column has at least one cross-contraction and its union support has at most five labels. A column supported on exactly five labels has two distinct-target commutator transvections and exactly one contraction; all five labels are distinct and it has form a_i;pk wedge a_p;qr, up to swapping factors/signs. The integral dummy-exchange relation from agent4_degree2_relations.md replaces it by a_i;qk wedge a_q;qr, supported on four labels. Thus every original column is, modulo true relations in ker q, zero or a column supported on at most four labels.

We now canonicalize each resulting column using only relations supported on at most four labels. It suffices to do this weight by weight. The possible nonzero weights in Hom(H,L_3) are (I) exactly one coefficient -1, all others nonnegative; (II) 2e_a; (III) e_a+e_b, a!=b. For any other weight B is zero and every reduced column is a local relation, hence q-zero.

## I: One negative coefficient

Write the weight as -e_i plus three positive letters with multiplicity, none equal to i. The output space is the corresponding multihomogeneous component of the free Lie ring on these positive letters, at target i. If the three letters are distinct a,b,c, an integral basis is [[a,b],c], [[a,c],b]. Both are images, up to sign, of local columns a_i;a c wedge a_a;a b and a_i;a b wedge a_a;a c. If the letters are a,a,b, the output is rank one, generated by [a,[a,b]], which is the image up to sign of a_i;a b wedge a_b;a b. Three identical letters give zero. Choose these columns as canonical lifts of a free basis.

For any reduced column, express its image in this integral basis. Subtract the corresponding canonical lifts. The difference is supported on at most four labels: the actual weight support has size four in the distinct-letter case and size three in the repeated-letter case, while the reduced column has at most four labels and contains the actual weight support. Its image is zero, so local injectivity proves the required equality in gr_2. The canonical images are independent. Therefore J_2 is injective on this weight.

## II: Weight 2e_a

The codomain weight has basis T_i=e_i^*[[X_i,X_a],X_a], i!=a. Every K--K column of this weight consists of two conjugations by X_a and commutes exactly. Every remaining nonzero column has form E_ip=a_i;p a wedge a_p;i a, with i,p distinct from a; its image is -T_i+T_p. Fix any anchor j!=a and take E_ji as canonical star columns, i!=a,j. Their images T_i-T_j are independent. The difference E_ip-(E_jp-E_ji) has zero image and is supported on {a,i,p,j}, at most four labels; terms with repeated indices are interpreted as zero and skew signs. Therefore local injectivity expresses every column in these independent star columns. J_2 is injective on this weight.

## III: Weight e_a+e_b, a!=b

For s outside {a,b}, put U_s=e_s^*[[X_s,X_a],X_b] and V_s=e_s^*[[X_s,X_b],X_a]. Put Z_a=e_a^*[X_a,[X_a,X_b]] and Z_b=e_b^*[[X_a,X_b],X_b]. These form an integral codomain basis. Use the actual columns

W_s=a_s;s a wedge a_s;s b,
L_s=a_s;a b wedge a_a;a s,
G=a_a;a b wedge a_b;a b.

Their images are respectively U_s-V_s, U_s+Z_a, and -Z_a+Z_b. These images are independent and form the full integral kernel of the functional sending every U_s,V_s to +1 and Z_a,Z_b to -1. This follows directly by solving coefficients at U_s,V_s, then at Z_a,Z_b; equivalently the corresponding minors have gcd one.

This functional is the symmetric trace on this weight. Define trace on an associative expansion of D(X_t) by contracting its first letter with t and symmetrizing the remaining two letters. It gives

Tr(e_t^*[[u,v],w])=delta_tu vw-delta_tv uw,
Tr(e_t^*[u,[v,w]])=-delta_tv uw+delta_tw uv.

For D=a_i;jk and E=a_p;qr, the bracket is delta_iq e_p^*[[j,k],r]+delta_ir e_p^*[q,[j,k]]-delta_pj e_i^*[[q,r],k]-delta_pk e_i^*[j,[q,r]]. Its trace is delta_iq(delta_pj kr-delta_pk jr)+delta_ir(-delta_pj qk+delta_pk qj)-delta_pj(delta_iq rk-delta_ir qk)-delta_pk(-delta_iq jr+delta_ir jq), which cancels termwise in the symmetric square. Thus Tr([D,E])=0 integrally, in all ranks. The script agent4_trace_certificate.py verifies this exactly for every pair of degree-one basis derivations through n=8 (41,250 pairs), as well as all W_s,L_s,G signs. The displayed formulas give the general proof independently of these finite tests.

For a reduced column supported on T, with |T|<=4 and {a,b} subset T, its trace-zero image therefore has a unique integral expression in G and those W_s,L_s for s in T minus {a,b}. Subtract that expression from the column. The result has zero image and support within T, so local rank<=4 injectivity makes it a true relation. Thus all columns are expressed in the globally independent G,W_s,L_s. J_2 is injective on this weight.

## Conclusion

Every integral weight has zero Johnson kernel, hence J_2:gr_2(IA_n)->Hom(H,L_3) is injective for every n>=2. Equivalently gamma_2(IA_n) intersect A_3(n)=gamma_3(IA_n). Combined with the degree-one theorem A_2=gamma_2, this proves A_3(n)=gamma_3(IA_n) for all n.

This establishes only c=2 of the requested all-rank low-degree range. It does not establish c=3,4,5 or any high-degree noninjectivity.

 Metaplectic congruence filtration lemma.
Let K be a nonarchimedean local field containing mu_p, O its valuation ring, pi a uniformizer, and C=p v_K(p)/(p-1). Let 1 -> mu_p -> H -> SL_infinity(K) -> 1 be the central extension obtained by pushing the stable Steinberg extension out through the Hilbert p-symbol. Use canonical root lifts x_ij(a), and standard torus lifts h_i,ell(u). The field Steinberg relations imply:
(i) root subgroups are additive; nonopposite root commutators have product parameter ab;
(ii) torus-root conjugation is the ordinary root-weight scaling;
(iii) torus commutators are Hilbert symbols, with exponent the integral Cartan pairing;
(iv) opposite-root Gaussian collection has possible central factor a Dennis-Stein symbol, whose Hilbert image is (1+ab,+-a)_p (with harmless inverse/sign according to conventions).
All signs in (iv) are harmless here since (-1,x)_p=1.

Local reciprocity gives (U_r,U_s)_p=1 when r+s>C, and U_{C+1} is contained in K^{*p}.
For r>C, define F_r to be the subgroup generated by x_ij(pi^r O) and h_i,ell(U_r), without adjoining mu_p. Gaussian collection gives F_r -> Gamma_r is an isomorphism: all cross-root pivots are in U_{2r}, hence are p-th powers, so (iv) contributes no center; torus symbols (iii) also vanish. Thus collection is exactly ordinary LDU collection, with unique normal form. In particular F_r intersects mu_p trivially.
For r<=C define F_r to be the full inverse image of Gamma_r.

Each deep F_r (r>C) is normalized by F_1. Verify this on the above generating roots and tori: nonopposite-root and torus-root commutators have parameter in pi^{r+1}; opposite-root pivots are in U_{r+1}, hence p-th powers; torus pairs U_r,U_1 have total depth>C. No central discrepancy remains.
More generally, if r+s>C, the same generator check yields [F_r,F_s] <= F_{r+s}: opposite-root pivots 1+ab lie in U_{r+s} and hence are p-th powers; torus pairs U_r,U_s pair trivially. If r+s<=C, the inclusion follows just from the ordinary matrix congruence commutator inclusion, as F_{r+s} is the full inverse image. Therefore (F_r) is an N-series.

Consequently Q=F_1/F_{C+1} is nilpotent of class at most C, and its central mu_p is still injective. All assertions hold in each finite rank >=3 and compatibly under stabilization. Q itself can be infinite-rank; each finitely generated image is a finite p-group since its projection is a congruence quotient over the finite ring O/pi^{C+1}.

CAVEAT FOR FINAL WRITEUP: relation (iv) and Gaussian uniqueness must be presented from the usual Steinberg/Dennis-Stein identities rather than assumed unexplained. The argument above gives the exact valuation verification once those standard identities are stated.

For g in Gamma_i and h in Gamma_j with i+j>C one has

addition has no central discrepancy. Nonopposite roots contribute a root
parameter ab, of valuation at least i+j. Torus/root interchange contributes

of p-th powers. Subsequent collection of the new level-(i+j) factors has
no central errors by the same argument. This verifies the displayed identities.
For products wholly at level r>C, the identical calculation establishes
multiplicativity of sigma. In these assertions all roots and tori appearing
in original LDU factors retain their indicated valuation bounds.

Set F_r=the full preimage of Gamma_r when 1<=r<=C and
F_r=sigma(Gamma_r) for r>C. Then [F_i,F_j] subset F_{i+j}:

### agent3_n3_proof.txt 
 Rank-three strictness, complete.
Write x1,x2,x3 for free generators. Set Kij(xi)=xj xi xj^{-1}, and Ci;jk(xi)=[xj,xk]xi; all other generators fixed. These are the nine Magnus generators of IA3.
Let d,e,f be degree-one derivations corresponding to K12,C1;23,C3;12. Their nonzero images are d(X1)=[X2,X1], e(X1)=[X2,X3], f(X3)=[X1,X2]. Set h=[e,f]. Then h(X1)=-[X2,[X1,X2]], h(X3)=[[X2,X3],X2], h(X2)=0. Direct derivation computation and Jacobi give [d,h]=0. Therefore w3=[K12,[C1;23,C3;12]] belongs gamma3(IA3) intersect A4(3). Define w_{c+1}=[K12,w_c]. Strong centrality gives w_c in gamma_c intersect A_{c+1} for every c>=3.

Detection in the infinite dihedral group:
The abelianized Fox Jacobian gives an antihomomorphism IA3 -> GL3(Z[t1^+-1,t2^+-1,t3^+-1]). Specialize all ti=-1. Every resulting matrix fixes (1,1,1)^T, by the Fox fundamental identity; quotient by this fixed line, using coordinates v1-v3,v2-v3, yields 2x2 matrices. Put
U=[[1,2],[0,1]], V=[[1,0],[2,1]], R=diag(-1,1), Z=-I.
In Magnus generator order K12,K13,C1;23,K21,K23,C2;13,K31,K32,C3;12, the matrices are
UR,R,U,ZVR,ZR,V,VR,ZUR,ZVU^{-1}.
Each identity is checked exactly in agent3_n3_checks.py. The subgroup <U,V> is free on U,V: on P1(R), put A={|z|>1}, B={|z|<1}; for every nonzero integer k, U^k(B) subset A and V^k(A) subset B. Ping-pong proves freeness and also excludes -I from <U,V>. R has determinant -1 and conjugates U,V to their inverses. Therefore <U,V,R,Z> is (F(U,V) semidirect C2_R) times C2_Z, with R inverting both free generators.
It has quotient D=<a,b | a^2=b^2=1> by U->a,V->b,R->1,Z->1. Inverting the row Jacobian first turns the antihomomorphism into a homomorphism q:IA3->D. On the nine Magnus generators q has images a,1,a,b,1,b,b,a,ab. Consequently q(w3)=[a,[a,ab]], equal (ab)^4 or its inverse depending on commutator convention; with the stated convention it is (ab)^4. In either case its exponent is +/-4.
Let z=ab. D is <z> semidirect <a>, with a z a=z^{-1}; its lower central series is gamma_c(D)=<z^{2^{c-1}}> for c>=2. Thus q(w3) is in gamma3(D) but not gamma4(D). Iterating [a,-] doubles the exponent up to sign, so q(w_c)=z^{+/-2^{c-1}} is not in gamma_{c+1}(D). It follows w_c not in gamma_{c+1}(IA3), proving strictness for n=3 and all c>=3.

No claim is made here about survival under IA3 -> IAn. That stabilization is unresolved in this team's work.


### agent3_metaplectic_route.txt 
 Candidate complete stable detector using wild metaplectic covers. NEED TEAM VERIFICATION of local-cover filtration lemma below; all other steps are standard or explicit.

Fix c>=3. If c has an odd prime divisor p, put k=c/p and take a totally ramified degree-k extension of Q_p(zeta_p); e=(p-1)k and residue field F_p. If c is a power of 2, c>=4; take a totally ramified extension of Q_2(i) of degree c/4; e=c/2. In both cases K contains mu_p, C=pe/(p-1)=c. For p=2, -1 is a square in K. Let pi be a uniformizer and t=1+pi.

Local Hilbert theorem: the pth Hilbert symbol on units satisfies (U_r,U_s)_p=1 if r+s>C, while U_r/U_{r+1} pairs nondegenerately with U_{C-r}/U_{C-r+1} whenever p does not divide r. For residue F_p both quotients here (r=1,s=c-1) have order p, so (1+pi,1+alpha*pi^{c-1}+O(pi^c))_p !=1 for every alpha nonzero mod pi. The O(pi^c) perturbation is invisible since 1+c>C.

Let R=Z[t,t^-1]. Bass-Heller-Swan gives K1(R)=R^*=< -1,t >, hence SK1(R)=0, and K2(R) is (Z/2)^2 generated by {-1,-1} and {-1,t}. Stabilize any matrix g by diag(g,det(g)^-1), giving a hom GL(R)->E_infty(R). Choose lifts to St(R), map t to 1+pi in St(K), then push its central K2(K) through the Hilbert symbol to mu_p. The image of K2(R) dies: it has exponent 2 for p odd, and both symbol generators die for p=2 since -1 is square. Consequently this procedure is a well-defined group hom GL(R)-> the mu_p metaplectic cover of SL_infty(K).

On a fixed finite rank N>=3 containing the relevant matrices, let K_r=ker(SL_N(O)->SL_N(O/pi^r)). The image of the Laurent congruence group lies over K1. Use Gaussian decomposition to select a section sigma on K1, made of ordered elementary root lifts and diagonal-torus lifts. CLAIM/LEMMA: sigma(K_{c+1}) is a normal subgroup of the preimage of K1 disjoint from mu_p, and the quotient Q is nilpotent of class at most c. Collection proof: for g in K_r,h in K_s, commutator equals a central factor times sigma([g,h]); if r+s>c the central factor is 1. Every central factor from Gaussian collection is either a Hilbert symbol of units in U_a,U_b with a+b>=r+s, or a symbol whose first entry is in U_{r+s} (hence is a pth power if r+s>c). The same argument handles product cocycles for sigma(K_{c+1}) and conjugation by K1. Repeated commutators have matrix part in K_r; the (c+1)st commutator has no central factor and lies sigma(K_{c+1}). Thus gamma_{c+1}(Q)=1 and mu_p survives.

Exact IA representation: character chi(x2)=1, chi(xi)=0 for i!=2 has kernel N. IA preserves chi and acts R-linearly on N_ab, a free R-module of rank n-1 with basis xi (i!=2). Image is G_{n-1}=<D_i(t),E_ij(t-1)>: K_i2 maps D_i(t); C_i;2j maps E_ij(t-1), while other Magnus generators map identity. If chosen Fox conventions invert these matrices, change signs/t inverses; none affect the argument.

Choose i=1,j=3 (indices excluding 2), and D=K12, A=C1;23, B=C3;12. Set B_k=ad_D^k(B) for group commutators, and w_c=[D,[A,B_{c-3}]]. Derivation calculation proves w_c in gamma_c(IA_n) intersect A_{c+1}(n) (agent1 has formulas).
Under the Laurent representation write s=t-1, D=diag_i(t), A=E_ij(s), B=E_ji(epsilon*s). Then B_k=E_ji(epsilon*(-1)^k*s^{k+1}*t^{-k}) exactly. For k=c-3 let a=s, b=epsilon*(-1)^k*s^{k+1}*t^{-k}, so ab has valuation c-1 and leading coefficient +/-1. The 2x2 commutator matrix is [[1+ab+(ab)^2,-a^2*b],[a*b^2,1-ab]]. Its Gaussian decomposition is a diagonal h_ij(u), u=1+ab+(ab)^2, times roots of depth >=c. Any central factor in its lift commutes with D. Commuting the root corrections with D moves them to depth >=c+1, hence they die in Q. Stabilized D is the torus h_ir(t) with a third index r, and the Steinberg torus relation gives [h_ir(t),h_ij(u)] equal (t,u)_p^{+/-1}, because the Cartan pairing is 1. This is nontrivial by the local unit-pairing theorem. Thus w_c has nontrivial central image in Q, but gamma_{c+1}(Q)=1, proving w_c not in gamma_{c+1}(IA_n).

Main possible flaw: the asserted Gaussian local-cover filtration lemma must be verified in detail; naive canonical sections may have central commutator factors at levels lower than r+s due arbitrary diagonal choices. Expected known statement is that p-metaplectic principal-congruence cover has nilpotence class c modulo deep canonical splitting, with sharp class c from torus pairing.


### agent4_base_derivation.txt 
 Exact initial Johnson calculation for n=3 base witness.

Write X=X1,Y=X2,Z=X3 in free Lie ring L(X,Y,Z), with usual bracket.
Let D=D1(K12), A=D1(C1;23), B=D1(C3;12), where K12 conjugates
x1 by x2 and C_i;jk multiplies xi by [xj,xk] on either chosen side.
Then
 D(X)=[Y,X], D(Y)=D(Z)=0;
 A(X)=[Y,Z], A(Y)=A(Z)=0;
 B(Z)=[X,Y], B(X)=B(Y)=0.
Set E=[A,B]. By direct derivation rule,
 E(X)=-[Y,[X,Y]]=[Y,[Y,X]]=ad_Y^2(X),
 E(Y)=0,
 E(Z)=[[Y,Z],Y]=-[Y,[Y,Z]]=-ad_Y^2(Z).
Therefore
 [D,E](X)=ad_Y^3(X)-ad_Y(ad_Y^2(X))=0,
 [D,E](Y)=0,
 [D,E](Z)=0.
Thus [D,[A,B]]=0 identically over Z, not just modulo a prime.
The graded Johnson map is a Lie homomorphism, so for the actual
commutator w=[K12,[C1;23,C3;12]] we have w in gamma3(IA3) intersect A4.

For the D_infinity quotient rho supplied by agent3, rho(K12)=a,
rho(C1;23)=a,rho(C3;12)=ab with a^2=b^2=1.
Exact reduction gives rho(w)=[a,[a,ab]]=(ab)^4.
Let T=ab. Since gamma_c(D_infinity)=<T^(2^(c-1))> for every c>=2,

Define w3=w and w_{c+1}=[K12,w_c]. Then w_c belongs to gamma_c(IA3)
intersect A_{c+1}, by strong centrality, while rho(w_c)=T^(4*(-2)^(c-3)).
This generates gamma_c(D_infinity), hence lies outside gamma_{c+1}.
Consequently strictness holds for n=3 and every c>=3.
